## Parameters

A test's `param()` block lists the values a user can tune per tenant: thresholds, switches, objects to exclude.
Values come from the run configuration or from `Invoke-MtTest -Parameter`; a test always has to run with none
set, using its defaults.

```powershell
param(
    # Longest validity period, in days, that a certificate may be issued for.
    [ValidateRange(1, 3650)]
    [int] $MaximumValidityDays = 365,

    # Members of these groups are exempt from this check.
    [MaesterParameter(Kind = 'Entra.Group')]
    [string[]] $ExcludedGroups,

    # How strictly to evaluate.
    [ValidateSet('Strict', 'Lenient')]
    [string] $Mode = 'Strict'
)
```

Rules:

- Types are `int`, `bool`, `switch`, `string` or `string[]`.
- Defaults are constants. No parameter is mandatory.
- Every parameter has a description: a `#` comment on the line directly above it, or `.PARAMETER` help. Only
  the comment line nearest the parameter is read, so keep the comment to one line or use `.PARAMETER`.
  `Get-MtTest` shows the description.
- Give thresholds a `ValidateRange`. A `ValidateSet` makes the parameter a list of choices.
- `Instance` and every name that starts with `Mt` belong to the engine and cannot be set.

Set values in the config:

```json
{
  "TestSettings": [
    { "Id": "CONTOSO.1002", "Parameters": { "ReasonMarker": "Off:" } },
    { "Id": "MT.1198", "Parameters": { "MaximumValidityDays": 180 } }
  ]
}
```

The engine checks each value against the `param()` block before the test runs. A name the test does not have,
a fraction for an `int`, a number for a `string`, a string for a `bool` or `switch`, or a value outside the
`ValidateRange` or `ValidateSet` gives that test an `Error` row with reason `InvalidConfiguration`; the run
carries on. A `string[]` parameter accepts one string or a list. The effective values, and where each came from
(`Default`, `Config` or `Parameter`), are written to the result row's `Parameters`.

### Parameter kinds

`[MaesterParameter(Kind = '...')]` says what a string parameter holds, so a user interface can offer a picker
and the engine can check the value's shape:

| Kind | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `Entra.User` | User object ID |
| `Entra.Group` | Group object ID |
| `Entra.ServicePrincipal` | Service principal object ID |
| `Entra.Application` | Application object ID |
| `Entra.ConditionalAccessPolicy` | Conditional Access policy ID |
| `Entra.NamedLocation` | Named location ID |
| `Entra.Domain` | Domain name |
| `Entra.DirectoryRole` | Directory role definition ID |
| `Azure.Subscription` | Subscription ID |
| `Azure.ResourceGroup` | Resource group ID (`/subscriptions/<id>/resourceGroups/<name>`) |
| `Azure.Resource` | Azure resource ID |

A value that does not match the kind's pattern (for example a malformed GUID) is `InvalidConfiguration`. In the
config a value can be the ID itself or an object `{ "Id": "...", "DisplayName": "..." }`; the test always
receives the ID.

[`Add-MtTestResultDetail`](../commands/Add-MtTestResultDetail.mdx) works as in 2.x. The parameters you use in a
native test:

- `-Result`: the Markdown result. It replaces `%TestResult%` in the `.md` file.
- `-GraphObjects` and `-GraphObjectType`: a list of objects rendered as a table with links to the admin
  portal, inserted where `%TestResult%` appears in `-Result`. See
  [Formatting test results](./formatting-test-results.md).
- `-Investigate`: the result needs a person to look at it.
- `-SkippedBecause`: skip the test for a reason only the test can see, such as `NotApplicable`,
  `NotSupportedAppPermission` or `Custom` with `-SkippedCustomReason`. Do not use the `NotConnected*` and
  `NotLicensed*` codes for conditions the attribute can declare; use `Service` and `License`.
- `-Description`: replaces the description from the `.md` file. Leave it out to use the `.md`.

`-TestTitle` and `-Severity` are ignored in a single-result native test: the title and severity come from the
attribute and the config. In a family, `-TestTitle` sets the instance's title when the instance object has no
`Title`. `-Severity` is used only when neither the config nor the attribute sets one.

### Embedding another tool's report

A test or a family's instance source that runs another tool can embed that tool's own single-file HTML report in
the Maester report with `Add-MtReportAttachment`:

```powershell
Add-MtReportAttachment -Name 'Zero Trust Assessment' -Path "$outputPath/ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html"
```

The report lists it near the bottom of the left menu (a pack's test's report goes in that pack's menu instead), and shows a button with that name on its overview page and
on the test's result (on every instance of a family). Each opens the embedded report in the main panel, beside the
Maester navigation, with a link to open it in a new browser tab. The attached report runs in a sandboxed frame
without access to the Maester report or its data. It works offline, so the Maester report stays one
file to share. The file is read and compressed at once, so you can delete the tool's output folder afterwards. The JSON
results file lists the attachment's name and size, not its content, and the HTML report leaves HTML attachments out
when `-RedactUserIdentity` is used.

With `-ContentType application/json`, an attachment is data for a view built into the report, which finds it by
its `Name` (the Zero Trust Assessment pack attaches its Zero Trust plan as `zero-trust-workshop`). It is not shown
as a button, and under `-RedactUserIdentity` it is redacted like the results instead of being left out.

### Errors and skips

Do not wrap the body in `try`/`catch` only to report `-SkippedBecause Error`. The engine runs every test inside
its own `try`, so any terminating error ends the test and becomes an `Error` row with the exception message as
`ReasonDetail` and the error record in `ErrorRecord`. Statement-terminating errors (a failed command, a method
call on `$null`) also end the test, so it cannot carry on with empty data and return `$true` by accident.

You may still use `try`/`catch` for a condition you handle, for example a 403 from Graph that you report as
`-SkippedBecause NotAuthorized`. A `-SkippedBecause` call made inside your own `try` block still skips the
test; the engine recognises the skip when your `catch` passes it to `Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause
Error -SkippedError $_`.

Warnings and non-terminating errors written by the test are shown on the console and stored on the result row
in `Diagnostics`.

## Declare what the test needs

Do not check connections or licences in the test. Declare them, and the engine decides before the test runs.
## Parameters

A test's `param()` block lists the values a user can tune per tenant: thresholds, switches, objects to exclude.
Values come from the run configuration or from `Invoke-MtTest -Parameter`; a test always has to run with none
set, using its defaults.

```powershell
param(
    # Longest validity period, in days, that a certificate may be issued for.
    [ValidateRange(1, 3650)]
    [int] $MaximumValidityDays = 365,

    # Members of these groups are exempt from this check.
    [MaesterParameter(Kind = 'Entra.Group')]
    [string[]] $ExcludedGroups,

    # How strictly to evaluate.
    [ValidateSet('Strict', 'Lenient')]
    [string] $Mode = 'Strict'
)
```

Rules:

- Types are `int`, `bool`, `switch`, `string` or `string[]`.
- Defaults are constants. No parameter is mandatory.
- Every parameter has a description: a `#` comment on the line directly above it, or `.PARAMETER` help. Only
  the comment line nearest the parameter is read, so keep the comment to one line or use `.PARAMETER`.
  `Get-MtTest` shows the description.
- Give thresholds a `ValidateRange`. A `ValidateSet` makes the parameter a list of choices.
- `Instance` and every name that starts with `Mt` belong to the engine and cannot be set.

Set values in the config:

```json
{
  "TestSettings": [
    { "Id": "CONTOSO.1002", "Parameters": { "ReasonMarker": "Off:" } },
    { "Id": "MT.1198", "Parameters": { "MaximumValidityDays": 180 } }
  ]
}
```

The engine checks each value against the `param()` block before the test runs. A name the test does not have,
a fraction for an `int`, a number for a `string`, a string for a `bool` or `switch`, or a value outside the
`ValidateRange` or `ValidateSet` gives that test an `Error` row with reason `InvalidConfiguration`; the run
carries on. A `string[]` parameter accepts one string or a list. The effective values, and where each came from
(`Default`, `Config` or `Parameter`), are written to the result row's `Parameters`.

`[MaesterParameter(Kind = '...')]` says what a string parameter holds, so a user interface can offer a picker
and the engine can check the value's shape:

| Kind | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `Entra.User` | User object ID |
| `Entra.Group` | Group object ID |
| `Entra.ServicePrincipal` | Service principal object ID |
| `Entra.Application` | Application object ID |
| `Entra.ConditionalAccessPolicy` | Conditional Access policy ID |
| `Entra.NamedLocation` | Named location ID |
| `Entra.Domain` | Domain name |
| `Entra.DirectoryRole` | Directory role definition ID |
| `Azure.Subscription` | Subscription ID |
| `Azure.ResourceGroup` | Resource group ID (`/subscriptions/<id>/resourceGroups/<name>`) |
| `Azure.Resource` | Azure resource ID |

A value that does not match the kind's pattern (for example a malformed GUID) is `InvalidConfiguration`. In the
config a value can be the ID itself or an object `{ "Id": "...", "DisplayName": "..." }`; the test always
receives the ID.

id: os_access_control_mobile_devices
title: Access Control for Mobile Devices
discussion: |-
  A mobile device is a computing device that has a small form factor such that it can easily be carried by a single individual; is designed to operate without a physical connection; possesses local, non-removable or removable data storage; and includes a self-contained power source. Mobile device functionality may also include voice communication capabilities, on-board sensors that allow the device to capture information, and/or built-in features for synchronizing local data with remote locations. Examples include smart phones and tablets. Mobile devices are typically associated with a single individual. The processing, storage, and transmission capability of the mobile device may be comparable to or merely a subset of notebook/desktop systems, depending on the nature and intended purpose of the device. Protection and control of mobile devices is behavior or policy-based and requires users to take physical action to protect and control such devices when outside of controlled areas. Controlled areas are spaces for which organizations provide physical or procedural controls to meet the requirements established for protecting information and systems.

  Due to the large variety of mobile devices with different characteristics and capabilities, organizational restrictions may vary for the different classes or types of such devices. Usage restrictions and specific implementation guidance for mobile devices include configuration management, device identification and authentication, implementation of mandatory protective software, scanning devices for malicious code, updating virus protection software, scanning for critical software updates and patches, conducting primary operating system (and possibly other resident software) integrity checks, and disabling unnecessary hardware.

  Usage restrictions and authorization to connect may vary among organizational systems. For example, the organization may authorize the connection of mobile devices to its network and impose a set of usage restrictions, while a system owner may withhold authorization for mobile device connection to specific applications or impose additional usage restrictions before allowing mobile device connections to a system.

  NOTE: The technology does not support this requirement. This is an applicable-does not meet finding.

input.content:
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Writes tests/frameworks/mscp.json, the catalogue of the NIST macOS Security Compliance Project (mSCP) rules, from a
checkout of usnistgov/macos_security.

.DESCRIPTION
The fleet compliance results of Jamf Pro's Compliance Benchmarks name each rule by its mSCP rule ID, such as
os_gatekeeper_enable. This catalogue lets Maester show each result under its rule, with the rule's CIS macOS, DISA
STIG, NIST SP 800-53, NIST SP 800-171 and CMMC references.

Only identifiers and facts are written: the rule ID, its section, the mSCP baselines it is in and its references.
No rule text is copied. mSCP is licensed CC BY 4.0 (Apple's vendor description text excluded); the pack's README
gives the attribution.

Needs the powershell-yaml module: Install-PSResource powershell-yaml.

.PARAMETER MscpPath
A checkout of https://github.com/usnistgov/macos_security.

.PARAMETER MacOSVersion
The macOS major version whose CIS benchmark and DISA STIG references are written as Related references.

.EXAMPLE
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/usnistgov/macos_security ../macos_security
./build/Update-MscpFramework.ps1 -MscpPath ../macos_security
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $MscpPath,
    [Parameter()] [ValidatePattern('^\d{2}$')] [string] $MacOSVersion = '26'
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Import-Module powershell-yaml

$root = (Resolve-Path $MscpPath).Path
$rulesPath = Join-Path $root 'rules'
if (-not (Test-Path $rulesPath)) { throw "$MscpPath has no rules folder. Point -MscpPath at a checkout of usnistgov/macos_security." }

# The release, for the framework's version: the newest heading of the changelog, such as "mSCP 2.0 Release 27.1".
$version = $null
$changelog = Join-Path $root 'CHANGELOG.md'
if (Test-Path $changelog) {
    $heading = Select-String -LiteralPath $changelog -Pattern '^#+\s*\[?([^\]\r\n]*Release[^\]\r\n]*|v?\d+\.\d+[^\]\r\n]*)' | Select-Object -First 1
    if ($heading) { $version = $heading.Matches[0].Groups[1].Value.Trim() }
}
if (-not $version) { $version = (git -C $root describe --tags --always 2>$null) }
if (-not $version) { throw 'Could not read the mSCP release from CHANGELOG.md or git.' }

# The baselines each rule is in, from the macOS baselines of this macOS version.
$baselineOf = @{}
$baselineFiles = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath (Join-Path $root 'baselines/macos') -Filter "*_macos_$MacOSVersion.0.yaml" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
foreach ($file in $baselineFiles) {
    $name = $file.BaseName -replace "_macos_$MacOSVersion\.0$", ''
    if ($name -eq 'all_rules') { continue }
    $baseline = Get-Content -LiteralPath $file.FullName -Raw | ConvertFrom-Yaml
    foreach ($section in $baseline.profile) {
        foreach ($rule in $section.rules) {
            if (-not $baselineOf.ContainsKey($rule)) { $baselineOf[$rule] = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new() }
            $baselineOf[$rule].Add($name)
        }
    }
}
if ($baselineOf.Count -eq 0) { throw "No macOS $MacOSVersion baselines in $root/baselines/macos. Pick another -MacOSVersion." }

$requirements = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
$files = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $rulesPath -Filter '*.yaml' -Recurse -FollowSymlink
foreach ($file in ($files | Sort-Object Name)) {
    $rule = Get-Content -LiteralPath $file.FullName -Raw | ConvertFrom-Yaml
    if (-not $rule.id -or -not $rule.platforms -or -not $rule.platforms.ContainsKey('macOS')) { continue }
    $refs = $rule.references
    $related = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
    foreach ($c in @($refs.nist.'800-53r5')) { if ($c -and $c -ne 'N/A') { $related.Add("nist-800-53-r5:$c") } }
    foreach ($c in @($refs.nist.'800-171r3')) { if ($c -and $c -ne 'N/A') { $related.Add("nist-800-171-r3:$c") } }
    foreach ($c in @($refs.disa.cmmc)) { if ($c -and $c -ne 'N/A') { $related.Add("cmmc-2:$c") } }
    $cisLevel = $null
    foreach ($c in @($refs.cis.benchmark."macos_$MacOSVersion")) {
        if ($c -match '^\s*([\d.]+)\s*(\(level (\d)\))?') {
            $related.Add("cis-apple-macos-$($MacOSVersion):$($Matches[1])")
            if ($Matches[3]) { $cisLevel = "L$($Matches[3])" }
        }
    }
    foreach ($c in @($refs.disa.disa_stig."macos_$MacOSVersion")) { if ($c -and $c -ne 'N/A') { $related.Add("disa-apple-macos-$MacOSVersion-stig:$c") } }
    foreach ($c in @($refs.cis.controls_v8)) { if ($c -and $c -ne 'N/A') { $related.Add("cis-controls-v8:$c") } }

    $requirement = [ordered]@{ Id = [string]$rule.id; Section = $file.Directory.Name }
    if ($baselineOf.ContainsKey($rule.id)) { $requirement.Baselines = @($baselineOf[$rule.id] | Sort-Object -Unique) }
    if ($cisLevel) { $requirement.CisLevel = $cisLevel }
    if ($related.Count) { $requirement.Related = @($related | Select-Object -Unique) }
    $requirements.Add($requirement)
}

$framework = [ordered]@{
    Framework    = 'mscp'
    Name         = 'NIST macOS Security Compliance Project'
    Version      = $version
    Url          = 'https://github.com/usnistgov/macos_security'
    License      = 'CC BY 4.0. Includes contributions from the US Government, the public and Apple Inc.'
    Requirements = $requirements
}
$out = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '../tests/frameworks/mscp.json'
$null = New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path (Split-Path $out) -Force
$framework | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $out -Encoding utf8NoBOM
Write-Host "Wrote $($requirements.Count) macOS rules of mSCP $version to $out."

    foreach ($c in @($refs.nist.'800-171r3')) { if ($c -and $c -ne 'N/A') { $related.Add("nist-800-171-r3:$c") } }
    foreach ($c in @($refs.disa.cmmc)) { if ($c -and $c -ne 'N/A') { $related.Add("cmmc-2:$c") } }
    $cisLevel = $null
    foreach ($c in @($refs.cis.benchmark."macos_$MacOSVersion")) {
        if ($c -match '^\s*([\d.]+)\s*(\(level (\d)\))?') {
            $related.Add("cis-apple-macos-$($MacOSVersion):$($Matches[1])")
            if ($Matches[3]) { $cisLevel = "L$($Matches[3])" }
        }
    }
    foreach ($c in @($refs.disa.disa_stig."macos_$MacOSVersion")) { if ($c -and $c -ne 'N/A') { $related.Add("disa-apple-macos-$MacOSVersion-stig:$c") } }
    foreach ($c in @($refs.cis.controls_v8)) { if ($c -and $c -ne 'N/A') { $related.Add("cis-controls-v8:$c") } }

    $requirement = [ordered]@{ Id = [string]$rule.id; Section = $file.Directory.Name }
    if ($baselineOf.ContainsKey($rule.id)) { $requirement.Baselines = @($baselineOf[$rule.id] | Sort-Object -Unique) }
    if ($cisLevel) { $requirement.CisLevel = $cisLevel }
    if ($related.Count) { $requirement.Related = @($related | Select-Object -Unique) }
    $requirements.Add($requirement)
}

$framework = [ordered]@{
    Framework    = 'mscp'
    Name         = 'NIST macOS Security Compliance Project'
    Version      = $version
    Url          = 'https://github.com/usnistgov/macos_security'
    License      = 'CC BY 4.0. Includes contributions from the US Government, the public and Apple Inc.'
    Requirements = $requirements
}
$out = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '../tests/frameworks/mscp.json'
$null = New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path (Split-Path $out) -Force
$framework | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $out -Encoding utf8NoBOM
Write-Host "Wrote $($requirements.Count) macOS rules of mSCP $version to $out."

Fact-checked on 2026-11-09. Every reference page used here was downloaded as raw OpenAPI Markdown (`https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/<slug>.md`) and parsed for paths, `x-required-privileges`, parameters and schemas. The JPAPI reference pages declare `"version": "11.33.0"`. One example is https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/postoauthtoken.md. The Classic API reference pages declare `"version": "11.32.0"`, for example https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/findosxconfigurationprofilesbyid.md.

## Conventions

- **JPAPI** means `{server}/api/...`. **Classic** means `{server}/JSSResource/...`.
- **[PD]** is https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/privileges-and-deprecations.md. The page is dated `updatedAt: 2026-05-07`, so it predates some 11.33 changes.
  - It does not list `/v4/computers-inventory`.
  - It shows `/v3/computers-inventory` with deprecation "N/A". The v3 reference page disagrees: it says `deprecated: true`, `x-deprecation-date: 2026-07-14`.
  - When the two disagree, the endpoint's own reference page takes precedence.
  - [PD] also states: "Endpoints that have been deprecated … will continue to be accessible for a minimum of one year after deprecation."
- **[CP]** is https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/classic-api-minimum-required-privileges-and-endpoint-mapping (`updatedAt: 2026-05-19`). It writes Classic privileges in user-account style, for example "Read - Webhooks".
- **API role strings for Classic resources are UNVERIFIED.** Third-party setup guides use "Read macOS Configuration Profiles" and "Read iOS Configuration Profiles": https://docs.stackone.com/connectors/jamf/guides/link-account/oauth-2-0-api-client-credentials and https://amplifiersecurity.freshdesk.com/support/solutions/articles/156000014188-jamf-endpoint-management. The mobile profile string is therefore probably "Read iOS …", not "Read Mobile Device …". No source found for "Read Webhooks" or "Read Disk Encryption Configurations". Confirm all of them with `GET /api/v1/api-role-privileges`.
- **Paging.** The shared parameters are `page` (integer, default 0) and `page-size` (integer, default 100), with no maximum declared in any schema. Sort uses `sort=prop:asc|desc`, comma-separated. Filter uses `filter=<RSQL>`, but only where the endpoint declares it.
- **RSQL** (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/filtering-with-rsql.md):
  - Comparison operators: `==`, `!=`, `=lt=`/`<`, `=le=`/`<=`, `=gt=`/`>`, `=ge=`/`>=`, `=in=`, `=out=`.
  - `;` means AND and `,` means OR. AND binds tighter than OR, and parentheses group.
  - `*` is a wildcard with `==` and `!=`.
  - String comparisons ignore case.
  - "Null values are not returned as part of any comparisons", but empty strings are compared.
  - Some endpoint descriptions show `and` in their filter examples, for example `/v1/accounts`: `username=="admin" and accountStatus==Enabled`. Use `;`, which is the documented form.

---

## 0. Authentication, token lifetime, invalidation, rate limits, and cloud versus on-prem

### Token request

- **Endpoint.** `POST {server}/api/v1/oauth/token`, with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. It needs no authentication (`x-authentication-required: false`).
  - Request fields: `grant_type=client_credentials`, `client_id` and `client_secret` (all required), plus an optional `scope`. The scope is a space-delimited list of the client's own roles, for example `api-role:1 api-role:2`.
  - Response fields (all required):
    - `access_token`: string. The securityScheme `bearerFormat` is JWT.
    - `token_type`: "Bearer".
    - `scope`: string.
    - `expires_in`: integer seconds, which "will reflect the `accessTokenLifetimeSeconds` value configured on your API Client".
  - A 400 uses the RFC 6749 error format: `error`, `error_description`, `error_uri`.
  - Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/postoauthtoken.md. The page's securityScheme `ApiClient` has `tokenUrl: /api/v1/oauth/token`.
- **Other sources for the path.** Jamf's recipe calls `"${url}/api/v1/oauth/token"` (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/recipes/client-credentials-authorization.md). [PD] lists `/v1/oauth/token` POST, privilege None, not deprecated.
- **Legacy path.** Jamf's blog says to use "the `/api/oauth/token` endpoint" (https://www.jamf.com/blog/understanding-jamf-pro-api-roles-and-clients/). Neither [PD] nor the 11.33 spec contains `/oauth/token` without `v1`. Use `/api/v1/oauth/token`. Whether the unversioned path still works is UNVERIFIED.
- **Version support.** From 10.49.0, "both the Classic and Jamf Pro APIs now support Client Credentials based authorization". "Access tokens can be used to interact with API endpoints in both the Classic and Jamf Pro APIs." Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/client-credentials.md

### Roles, secrets and lifetime

- **Role and secret changes.** "Adding or removing an API Role from an existing API Client requires that the client secret be rotated for the changes to take effect. 1	# Jamf Pro read-only API research for the Maester Pack connector (checks 1–13), fact-checked
2	
3	Fact-checked on 2026-11-09. Every reference page used here was downloaded as raw OpenAPI Markdown (`https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/<slug>.md`) and parsed for paths, `x-required-privileges`, parameters and schemas. The pages are in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-merill--claude-spares-spare-w9QrxL/f671424e-6754-4173-963b-f24a1e0ad80d/scratchpad/jamf/ref/`. The privileges page is saved as `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-merill--claude-spares-spare-w9QrxL/f671424e-6754-4173-963b-f24a1e0ad80d/scratchpad/jamf/pd.md`.
4	
5	The JPAPI reference pages declare `"version": "11.33.0"`. One example is https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/postoauthtoken.md. The Classic API reference pages declare `"version": "11.32.0"`, for example https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/findosxconfigurationprofilesbyid.md.
6	
7	## Conventions
8	
9	- **JPAPI** means `{server}/api/...`. **Classic** means `{server}/JSSResource/...`.
10	- **[PD]** is https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/privileges-and-deprecations.md. The page is dated `updatedAt: 2026-05-07`, so it predates some 11.33 changes.
11	  - It does not list `/v4/computers-inventory`.
12	  - It shows `/v3/computers-inventory` with deprecation "N/A". The v3 reference page disagrees: it says `deprecated: true`, `x-deprecation-date: 2026-07-14`.
13	  - When the two disagree, the endpoint's own reference page takes precedence.
14	  - [PD] also states: "Endpoints that have been deprecated … will continue to be accessible for a minimum of one year after deprecation."
15	- **[CP]** is https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/classic-api-minimum-required-privileges-and-endpoint-mapping (`updatedAt: 2026-05-19`). It writes Classic privileges in user-account style, for example "Read - Webhooks".
16	- **API role strings for Classic resources are UNVERIFIED.** Third-party setup guides use "Read macOS Configuration Profiles" and "Read iOS Configuration Profiles": https://docs.stackone.com/connectors/jamf/guides/link-account/oauth-2-0-api-client-credentials and https://amplifiersecurity.freshdesk.com/support/solutions/articles/156000014188-jamf-endpoint-management. The mobile profile string is therefore probably "Read iOS …", not "Read Mobile Device …". No source found for "Read Webhooks" or "Read Disk Encryption Configurations". Confirm all of them with `GET /api/v1/api-role-privileges`.
17	- **Paging.** The shared parameters are `page` (integer, default 0) and `page-size` (integer, default 100), with no maximum declared in any schema. Sort uses `sort=prop:asc|desc`, comma-separated. Filter uses `filter=<RSQL>`, but only where the endpoint declares it.
18	- **RSQL** (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/filtering-with-rsql.md):
19	  - Comparison operators: `==`, `!=`, `=lt=`/`<`, `=le=`/`<=`, `=gt=`/`>`, `=ge=`/`>=`, `=in=`, `=out=`.
20	  - `;` means AND and `,` means OR. AND binds tighter than OR, and parentheses group.
21	  - `*` is a wildcard with `==` and `!=`.
22	  - String comparisons ignore case.
23	  - "Null values are not returned as part of any comparisons", but empty strings are compared.
24	  - Some endpoint descriptions show `and` in their filter examples, for example `/v1/accounts`: `username=="admin" and accountStatus==Enabled`. Use `;`, which is the documented form.
25	
26	---
27	
28	## 0. Authentication, token lifetime, invalidation, rate limits, and cloud versus on-prem
29	
30	### Token request
31	
32	- **Endpoint.** `POST {server}/api/v1/oauth/token`, with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. It needs no authentication (`x-authentication-required: false`).
33	  - Request fields: `grant_type=client_credentials`, `client_id` and `client_secret` (all required), plus an optional `scope`. The scope is a space-delimited list of the client's own roles, for example `api-role:1 api-role:2`.
34	  - Response fields (all required):
35	    - `access_token`: string. The securityScheme `bearerFormat` is JWT.
36	    - `token_type`: "Bearer".
37	    - `scope`: string.
38	    - `expires_in`: integer seconds, which "will reflect the `accessTokenLifetimeSeconds` value configured on your API Client".
39	  - A 400 uses the RFC 6749 error format: `error`, `error_description`, `error_uri`.
40	  - Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/postoauthtoken.md. The page's securityScheme `ApiClient` has `tokenUrl: /api/v1/oauth/token`.
41	- **Other sources for the path.** Jamf's recipe calls `"${url}/api/v1/oauth/token"` (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/recipes/client-credentials-authorization.md). [PD] lists `/v1/oauth/token` POST, privilege None, not deprecated.
42	- **Legacy path.** Jamf's blog says to use "the `/api/oauth/token` endpoint" (https://www.jamf.com/blog/understanding-jamf-pro-api-roles-and-clients/). Neither [PD] nor the 11.33 spec contains `/oauth/token` without `v1`. Use `/api/v1/oauth/token`. Whether the unversioned path still works is UNVERIFIED.
43	- **Version support.** From 10.49.0, "both the Classic and Jamf Pro APIs now support Client Credentials based authorization". "Access tokens can be used to interact with API endpoints in both the Classic and Jamf Pro APIs." Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/client-credentials.md
44	
45	### Roles, secrets and lifetime
46	
47	- **Role and secret changes.** "Adding or removing an API Role from an existing API Client requires that the client secret be rotated for the changes to take effect. Adding or removing a privilege from an API Role will immediately take effect for all newly generated access tokens." Source: the client-credentials guide above.
48	- **Secret retrieval.** "There is no way to retrieve an existing Client Secret, neither via the GUI nor the API." Source: the Jamf blog above.
49	- **Default lifetime.** The default `accessTokenLifetimeSeconds` is UNVERIFIED. No primary source states it. The OAuth reference page uses 60 as an example value, and the api-integrations page uses 300; neither is a default.
50	
51	### Invalidation
52	
53	- **Endpoint.** `POST /api/v1/auth/invalidate-token` with a Bearer token returns 204. [PD] lists privilege None and no deprecation.
54	  - Sources: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/post_v1-auth-invalidate-token.md and [PD].
55	  - Jamf's client-credentials recipe calls it with an OAuth token and checks for 204.
56	  - The legacy `POST /auth/invalidateToken` was deprecated on 2020-06-01 [PD].
57	- **Keep-alive.** `POST /api/v1/auth/keep-alive` exists (privilege None [PD]). A client-credentials pack should request a new token instead.
58	- **Basic auth.** Before 11.5.0, a username and password could call any Classic endpoint. From 11.5.0 they can only obtain a token, but an option in the UI could relax this. From 11.17.0 the restriction cannot be turned off. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/classic-api-authentication-changes.md
59	- **SSO.** "API authentication does not support the use of SSO." Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/jamf-pro-api-overview.md
60	
61	### Rate limits
62	
63	- **No built-in limit.** "Jamf Pro does not have a built-in solution to restrict or limit the number of API requests made over a given time interval."
64	- **Guidance.** "Limit your interactions with Jamf APIs to no more than 5 concurrent connections." Jamf recommends exponential backoff. For applications that do not need real-time data, run full inventory syncs "no more than once every 24 hours" and filter to devices that reported in the last day.
65	- Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/jamf-pro-api-scalability-best-practices.md
66	- **Load signal on Jamf Cloud.** `GET /api/v1/health-status` requires authentication but no privilege [PD].
67	  - It returns `{api, ui, enrollment, device, default}`. Each group holds `{thirtySeconds, oneMinute, fiveMinutes, fifteenMinutes, thirtyMinutes}`, all numbers.
68	  - Each value is an acceptance ratio from 0 to 1: "1 means all requests were accepted and 0 means all were denied". Jamf Cloud nodes do reject requests under load.
69	  - "Health status metrics are only available in Jamf Cloud". The documented responses are 200 and 404.
70	  - The status code returned for a denied request is UNVERIFIED; the page documents no 429 or 503.
71	  - Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-health-status.md
72	
73	### Cloud versus on-prem
74	
75	- **Detection.** `GET /api/v1/cloud-information` needs no authentication (`x-authentication-required: false`) and no privilege [PD]. It returns `{cloudInstance, rampInstance, fedRampInstance, govCloudInstance, managedServiceProviderInstance, highComplianceInstance, fipsEnabled}`, all booleans. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-cloud-information.md
76	- **Clustering.**
77	  - Jamf Cloud has "up to a 60 second delay" before new objects reach other nodes.
78	  - Sticky sessions use the `APBALANCEID` or `jpro-ingress` cookie. The name "may vary based on hosting region and infrastructure".
79	  - A read-only pack does not need them.
80	  - Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/sticky-sessions-for-jamf-cloud.md
81	  - The guide gives no cluster refresh interval. The earlier "refreshes every minute" claim is not supported by the page and has been removed.
82	- **Change Management export** is on-prem only. See section 12.
83	
84	---
85	
86	## 1. SSO settings
87	
88	- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v3/sso`
89	- **Privilege:** **Read SSO Settings** (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v3-sso.md; [PD])
90	- **`SsoSettingsV3` fields:**
91	  - `configurationType`: enum `SAML`, `OIDC`, `OIDC_WITH_SAML`
92	  - booleans, each defaulting to false: `ssoEnabled`, `ssoBypassAllowed`, `ssoForEnrollmentEnabled`, `ssoForMacOsSelfServiceEnabled`, `enrollmentSsoForAccountDrivenEnrollmentEnabled`, `groupEnrollmentAccessEnabled`
93	  - `groupEnrollmentAccessName`: string
94	  - `enrollmentSsoConfig`: `{hosts: [string], managementHint: string}`
95	- **`oidcSettings`:** `userMapping` (enum `USERNAME`, `EMAIL`), `jamfIdAuthenticationEnabled` (default true), `usernameAttributeClaimMapping` (enum `USERNAME`, `EMAIL`)
96	- **`samlSettings`:**
97	  - `idpProviderType`: enum `ADFS`, `OKTA`, `GOOGLE`, `SHIBBOLETH`, `ONELOGIN`, `PING`, `CENTRIFY`, `AZURE`, `OTHER`
98	  - `metadataSource`: enum `URL`, `FILE`, `UNKNOWN`
99	  - `sessionTimeout`: integer, default 480
100	  - `tokenExpirationDisabled`: boolean, default false
101	  - `userAttributeEnabled`: boolean
102	  - strings: `userAttributeName`, `userMapping` (enum `USERNAME`, `EMAIL`), `groupAttributeName` (default `http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/claims/Group`), `groupRdnKey`, `idpUrl`, `entityId`, `metadataFileName`, `otherProviderTypeName`, `federationMetadataFile`
103	- **What `ssoBypassAllowed` means:** the spec does not describe the field.
104	  - Jamf's documentation describes the "Allow users to bypass the Single Sign-On authentication" option: users can sign in without SSO when they go straight to the Jamf Pro URL. Without it, unauthenticated users are redirected to the IdP.
105	  - Sources: https://learn.jamf.com/r/en-US/jamf-pro-documentation-current/Enabling_Single_Sign-On_in_Jamf_Pro and https://learn.jamf.com/r/en-US/jamf-pro-documentation-11.29.0/SAML-Based_Single_Sign-On (seen in search summaries, not fully opened).
106	  - Mapping the field to this checkbox is an inference: UNVERIFIED-strong.
107	- **Failover login:** `GET /api/v1/sso/failover` returns 200 `{failoverUrl: string, generationTime: integer}`, or 400 "Failover url not generated". Privilege: **Read SSO Settings**. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-sso-failover.md
108	  - Reading this privilege reveals the failover URL itself. Treat the value as sensitive and do not log it.
109	- **Related:** `GET /api/v2/jamf-pro-information` returns `ssoSamlEnabled` among other booleans. It requires authentication but no privilege [PD]. Its `byodEnabled` field is deprecated as of 11.25. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v2-jamf-pro-information.md
110	- **STIG link:** V-241791 (medium) requires a session lock after 15 minutes of inactivity. `samlSettings.sessionTimeout` (default 480) relates to it; that this field is the session lock is UNVERIFIED. Source: https://cyber.trackr.live/api/stig/Jamf_Pro_v10.x_EMM/3/2
111	- **Sample (illustrative):**
112	  `{"configurationType":"SAML","ssoEnabled":true,"ssoBypassAllowed":false,"ssoForEnrollmentEnabled":true,"samlSettings":{"idpProviderType":"AZURE","sessionTimeout":480,"tokenExpirationDisabled":false},"oidcSettings":{"userMapping":"USERNAME"}}`
113	
114	## 2. API roles
115	
116	- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/api-roles`, and `/{id}` for one role
117	- **Privilege:** **Read API Roles** (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/getallapiroles.md; [PD])
118	- **Parameters:** `page`, `page-size`, `sort` (default `id:asc`; fields `id`, `displayName`) and `filter` (fields `id`, `displayName`, for example `displayName=="*myRole*"`)
119	- **Response:** `{totalCount: integer, results: [{id: string, displayName: string, privileges: [string]}]}`
120	- **Catalogue of all privileges:** `GET /api/v1/api-role-privileges` returns `{privileges: [string]}`. Privilege: **Read API Roles**. [PD] also lists `/v1/api-role-privileges/search`. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-api-role-privileges.md
121	- **Sample (illustrative):** `{"totalCount":1,"results":[{"id":"1","displayName":"Maester RO","privileges":["Read Computers","Read SSO Settings"]}]}`
122	
123	## 3. API integrations (API clients)
124	
125	- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/api-integrations`, and `/{id}` for one client
126	- **Privilege:** **Read API Integrations** (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-api-integrations.md; [PD])
127	- **Parameters:** `sort` (default `id:asc`) and `filter`; both accept `id` and `displayName`
128	- **`ApiIntegrationResponse` fields:**
129	  - `id`: integer
130	  - `displayName`: string
131	  - `enabled`: boolean
132	  - `authorizationScopes`: [string], the names of the assigned API roles
133	  - `appType`: enum `CLIENT_CREDENTIALS`, `NATIVE_APP_OAUTH`, `NONE`
134	  - `clientId`: string
135	  - `accessTokenLifetimeSeconds`: integer
136	- **Missing fields:** the schema has no created, last-used or secret-age field.
137	- **Sample (illustrative):** `{"totalCount":1,"results":[{"id":1,"displayName":"My API Integration","enabled":true,"authorizationScopes":["Maester RO"],"accessTokenLifetimeSeconds":300,"appType":"CLIENT_CREDENTIALS","clientId":"538878d4-..."}]}`
138	
139	## 4. Jamf Pro user accounts and groups
140	
141	### Accounts
142	
143	- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/accounts`
144	- **Privilege:** **Read Accounts** (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-accounts.md; [PD])
145	- **Sort and filter fields:** `id`, `lastPasswordChange`, `failedLoginAttempts`, `username`, `realname`, `email`, `phone`, `ldapServerId`, `distinguishedName`, `siteId`, `privilegeLevel`, `changePasswordOnNextLogin`, `accountStatus`
146	- **Default sort is inconsistent:** the schema default is `username:asc`, but the description says `username:desc`.
147	- **`UserAccount` fields:**
148	  - `id`: string
149	  - `username`, `realname`, `email`, `phone`, `distinguishedName`: string
150	  - `ldapServerId`: integer, default -1. Reading -1 as a local account is inferred from the default.
151	  - `siteId`: integer, default -1
152	  - `accessLevel`: enum `FullAccess`, `SiteAccess`, `GroupBasedAccess`
153	  - `privilegeLevel`: enum `ADMINISTRATOR`, `AUDITOR`, `ENROLLMENT`, `CUSTOM`
154	  - `lastPasswordChange`: date-time
155	  - `changePasswordOnNextLogin`: boolean
156	  - `failedLoginAttempts`: integer
157	  - `accountStatus`: enum `Enabled`, `Disabled`
158	  - `accountType`: enum `DEFAULT`, `FEDERATED`, `MIGRATED`
159	  - `plainPassword`: string, used for writes
160	- **Example filters:** `privilegeLevel==ADMINISTRATOR;accountStatus==Enabled`, or `ldapServerId==-1`
161	- **Sample (illustrative):** `{"totalCount":1,"results":[{"id":"1","username":"admin","ldapServerId":-1,"siteId":-1,"accessLevel":"FullAccess","privilegeLevel":"ADMINISTRATOR","lastPasswordChange":"2017-07-21T17:32:28Z","changePasswordOnNextLogin":false,"failedLoginAttempts":0,"accountStatus":"Enabled","accountType":"DEFAULT"}]}`
162	
163	### Groups
164	
165	- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/account-groups`
166	- **Privilege:** **Read Account Groups** (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-account-groups.md; [PD])
167	- **Parameters:** `sort` (default `name:asc`) and `filter`; fields `id`, `name`, `siteId`, `ldapServerId`
168	- **`AccountGroupV1` fields:**
169	  - `id`, `name`: string
170	  - `accessLevel`, `privilegeLevel`: same enums as accounts
171	  - `siteId`, `ldapServerId`, `directoryGroupId`: string
172	  - `members`: `[{id, username, realname, email}]`
173	  - `privileges`: [string], for example `["Read Computers","Update Computers"]`
174	
175	### Last login and sessions
176	
177	- **Per-account:** `UserAccount` has no last-login field.
178	- **`GET /api/v1/last-login`:** privilege **Read Last Login**. Returns 200 `{lastLogin: date-time}` or 204, and takes no parameters. The description says only "Returns the date of the last login event", so whose login it reports is UNVERIFIED. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-last-login.md
179	- **`GET /api/v1/user-sessions/active`:** privilege **Read User**. Returns `[{username, sessionId, lastAccessedTime, creationTime, userAgent, ipAddress}]`. [PD] also lists `/v1/user-sessions/count`. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-user-sessions-active.md
180	
181	### Classic alternative (not needed)
182	
183	- `GET /JSSResource/accounts/userid/{id}` returns:
184	  - `enabled` ("Enabled"/"Disabled")
185	  - `access_level` ("Full Access"/"Site Access"/"Group Access")
186	  - `privilege_set` ("Administrator"/"Auditor"/"Enrollment Only"/"Custom")
187	  - `directory_user`, `ldap_server{id,name}`, `force_password_change`
188	  - `privileges{jss_objects, jss_settings, jss_actions, recon, casper_admin, casper_remote, casper_imaging}`
189	- Classic privilege: "Read - User accounts and groups" [CP]
190	- Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/findaccountsbyid.md
191	
192	## 5. Console password policy and lockout
193	
194	- **No API endpoint was found.** The current JPAPI index (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/jamf-pro-api/llms.txt, 1,428 lines, re-downloaded 2026-11-09) has no password-policy or lockout resource. Neither does the Classic index (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/classic-api/llms.txt). The only password-related JPAPI items are LAPS, the recovery lock, `POST /v1/user/change-password` and PKI. Treat a password-policy API as UNVERIFIED; it probably does not exist.
195	- **Account preferences are not the policy.** `/api/v3/account-preferences` (privilege None [PD]) and `/api/v2/account-preferences` (deprecated 2025-06-30 [PD]) hold the caller's own UI preferences. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v3-account-preferences.md
196	- **What the policy covers in the UI.** It sets lockout attempts, self-unlock, password length, age, reuse and complexity, and applies only to local accounts. Source: https://learn.jamf.com/r/en-US/jamf-pro-documentation-11.16.0/Configuring_the_Password_Policy (not re-opened in this check; carried over).
197	- **Possible proxy signals:** `failedLoginAttempts`, `lastPasswordChange` and `changePasswordOnNextLogin` on `/api/v1/accounts`.
198	- **STIG values** (Jamf Pro v10.x EMM STIG; https://cyber.trackr.live/api/stig/Jamf_Pro_v10.x_EMM/3/2 reports `"published": "2026-09-02"`; all medium):
199	  - V-241804: password length of 15
200	  - V-241805 to V-241808: at least one lowercase, uppercase, number and special character
201	  - V-241809: minimum lifetime of 24 hours
202	  - V-241810: maximum lifetime of 6 months
203	  - V-241811: no reuse for 5 generations
204	  - V-241812: disable local accounts after 35 days inactive
205	  - V-241813: limit of 3 consecutive invalid attempts
206	  - V-241817: local accounts created during installation must be disabled

208	## 6. Server version and latest release
209	
210	- **Version:** `GET /api/v1/jamf-pro-version` returns `{version: string}`. Authentication is required but no privilege [PD]. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-jamf-pro-version.md
211	- **Latest release:** no API exists for it.
212	  - The documentation's "current" alias shows "Jamf Pro Documentation 11.33.0" (https://learn.jamf.com/r/en-US/jamf-pro-documentation-current/Change_Management).
213	  - Community announcements report 11.33 GA, 11.33.1 and 11.33.3. These are secondary and were not re-verified:
214	    - https://community.jamf.com/release-announcements-177/jamf-pro-11-33-now-available-58978
215	    - https://community.jamf.com/release-announcements-177/jamf-pro-11-33-3-now-available-59123
216	- **Supported-version policy:** Jamf's lifecycle policy is UNVERIFIED.
217	  - STIG V-241798 (high, rule SV-241798r971326_rule, JAMF-10-000700) requires a supported version.
218	  - Its check and fix text list v10.13.1 to v10.18 with end of support "TBD", and allow "a newer version than on the list". The list is stale. Source: https://cyber.trackr.live/api/stig/Jamf_Pro_v10.x_EMM/3/2/V-241798
219	  - Suggestion: a pack parameter for the minimum version.
220	- **Cloud versus on-prem:** Jamf manages Jamf Cloud upgrades, so this check matters mainly on-prem. Detect the deployment with `/api/v1/cloud-information`.

222	## 7. User-initiated enrollment
223	
224	- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v4/enrollment`
225	- **Privilege:** **Read User-Initiated Enrollment** (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v4-enrollment.md; [PD])
226	- **Enrollment toggles (booleans, defaults in parentheses):**
227	  - `macOsEnterpriseEnrollmentEnabled` (false)
228	  - `iosEnterpriseEnrollmentEnabled` (true)
229	  - `iosPersonalEnrollmentEnabled` (false)
230	  - `accountDrivenUserEnrollmentEnabled`
231	  - `accountDrivenDeviceIosEnrollmentEnabled`
232	  - `accountDrivenDeviceMacosEnrollmentEnabled`
233	  - `accountDrivenUserVisionosEnrollmentEnabled`
234	  - `accountDrivenDeviceVisionosEnrollmentEnabled`
235	- **Other fields:**
236	  - booleans: `installSingleProfile`, `signingMdmProfileEnabled`, `restrictReenrollment`, `flushLocationInformation`, `flushLocationHistoryInformation`, `flushPolicyHistory`, `flushExtensionAttributes`, `flushSoftwareUpdatePlans`, `createManagementAccount` (default true), `hideManagementAccount`, `allowSshOnlyManagementAccount`, `ensureSshRunning` (default true), `launchSelfService`, `signQuickAdd`, `maidUsernameMergeEnabled`

Added the fields `flushLocationInformation`, `flushLocationHistoryInformation`, `flushExtensionAttributes`, `flushSoftwareUpdatePlans` and `maidUsernameMergeEnabled`. The certificate and keystore fields are flagged as never to log. `personalDeviceEnrollmentType` was deprecated in 11.25 and always returns "USERENROLLMENT".
480	11. **SAML fields.** Added `userAttributeName`, `groupRdnKey`, `metadataFileName`, `otherProviderTypeName` and `federationMetadataFile`. `groupAttributeName` defaults to the ADFS group claim URI, and `usernameAttributeClaimMapping` is an enum `USERNAME`/`EMAIL`.
481	12. **Log flushing.** `retentionPeriodUnit` is a plain string with example values, not a declared enum.
482	13. **Classic profile fields.** `redeploy_on_update` is a string, for example "Newly Assigned". `general` also has `description`, `site` and `category`. The Classic spec version is 11.32.0.
483	14. **Classic webhooks.** The schema includes `password`, `enable_display_fields_for_group_object` and `display_fields`. `content_type` is `text/xml`|`application/json`. The pack should drop `password`.
484	15. **Mobile profile privilege.** The API role string is probably "Read iOS Configuration Profiles" (third-party), not "Mobile Device Configuration Profiles".
485	16. **Never-grant list.** Added the v4 secret endpoints: `/v4/computers-inventory/filevault`, `/v4/computers-inventory/{id}/view-recovery-lock-password` and `/v4/computers-inventory/{id}/view-device-lock-pin`. Also added "View Local Admin Password Audit History" and "Dismiss Notifications".
486	17. **New endpoint for STIG V-241794.** `GET /api/v1/login-customization` needs no privilege and reports `includeCustomDisclaimer` and the banner text.
487	18. **STIG gaps.** Added V-241791 (15-minute session lock), V-241794 (banner) and V-241817 (disable installation-time local accounts). V-241798 also has rule SV-241798r971326_rule and version JAMF-10-000700, and its stale version list appears in both the check text and the fix text.
488	19. **Basic auth before 11.17.** Between 11.5.0 and 11.17.0, an option in the UI could relax the token-only restriction.
489	20. **Missing privilege statements.** `/v1/notifications`, `/v1/health-status` and `/v2/jamf-pro-information` require authentication but no named privilege. "No privilege" does not mean no authentication.
490	21. **`/v2/jamf-pro-information`.** The endpoint is not deprecated; only its `byodEnabled` field is (11.25).
491	22. **Log Stream.** It covers Change Management and Access logs and is available only on Jamf Cloud Premium.
492	23. **Accounts filter example.** The `/v1/accounts` description uses `and` in its RSQL example, but the documented AND operator is `;`.

# Jamf Pro read-only API research for the Maester Pack connector (checks 1–13), fact-checked

Fact-checked on 2026-11-09. Every reference page used here was downloaded as raw OpenAPI Markdown (`https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/<slug>.md`) and parsed for paths, `x-required-privileges`, parameters and schemas. The pages are in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-merill--claude-spares-spare-w9QrxL/f671424e-6754-4173-963b-f24a1e0ad80d/scratchpad/jamf/ref/`. The privileges page is saved as `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-merill--claude-spares-spare-w9QrxL/f671424e-6754-4173-963b-f24a1e0ad80d/scratchpad/jamf/pd.md`.

The JPAPI reference pages declare `"version": "11.33.0"`. One example is https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/postoauthtoken.md. The Classic API reference pages declare `"version": "11.32.0"`, for example https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/findosxconfigurationprofilesbyid.md.

## Conventions

- **JPAPI** means `{server}/api/...`. **Classic** means `{server}/JSSResource/...`.
- **[PD]** is https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/privileges-and-deprecations.md. The page is dated `updatedAt: 2026-05-07`, so it predates some 11.33 changes.
  - It does not list `/v4/computers-inventory`.
  - It shows `/v3/computers-inventory` with deprecation "N/A". The v3 reference page disagrees: it says `deprecated: true`, `x-deprecation-date: 2026-07-14`.
  - When the two disagree, the endpoint's own reference page takes precedence.
  - [PD] also states: "Endpoints that have been deprecated … will continue to be accessible for a minimum of one year after deprecation."
- **[CP]** is https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/classic-api-minimum-required-privileges-and-endpoint-mapping (`updatedAt: 2026-05-19`). It writes Classic privileges in user-account style, for example "Read - Webhooks".
- **API role strings for Classic resources are UNVERIFIED.** Third-party setup guides use "Read macOS Configuration Profiles" and "Read iOS Configuration Profiles": https://docs.stackone.com/connectors/jamf/guides/link-account/oauth-2-0-api-client-credentials and https://amplifiersecurity.freshdesk.com/support/solutions/articles/156000014188-jamf-endpoint-management. The mobile profile string is therefore probably "Read iOS …", not "Read Mobile Device …". No source found for "Read Webhooks" or "Read Disk Encryption Configurations". Confirm all of them with `GET /api/v1/api-role-privileges`.
- **Paging.** The shared parameters are `page` (integer, default 0) and `page-size` (integer, default 100), with no maximum declared in any schema. Sort uses `sort=prop:asc|desc`, comma-separated. Filter uses `filter=<RSQL>`, but only where the endpoint declares it.
- **RSQL** (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/filtering-with-rsql.md):
  - Comparison operators: `==`, `!=`, `=lt=`/`<`, `=le=`/`<=`, `=gt=`/`>`, `=ge=`/`>=`, `=in=`, `=out=`.
  - `;` means AND and `,` means OR. AND binds tighter than OR, and parentheses group.
  - `*` is a wildcard with `==` and `!=`.
  - String comparisons ignore case.
  - "Null values are not returned as part of any comparisons", but empty strings are compared.
  - Some endpoint descriptions show `and` in their filter examples, for example `/v1/accounts`: `username=="admin" and accountStatus==Enabled`. Use `;`, which is the documented form.

---

## 0. Authentication, token lifetime, invalidation, rate limits, and cloud versus on-prem

### Token request

- **Endpoint.** `POST {server}/api/v1/oauth/token`, with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. It needs no authentication (`x-authentication-required: false`).
  - Request fields: `grant_type=client_credentials`, `client_id` and `client_secret` (all required), plus an optional `scope`. The scope is a space-delimited list of the client's own roles, for example `api-role:1 api-role:2`.
  - Response fields (all required):
    - `access_token`: string. The securityScheme `bearerFormat` is JWT.
    - `token_type`: "Bearer".
    - `scope`: string.
    - `expires_in`: integer seconds, which "will reflect the `accessTokenLifetimeSeconds` value configured on your API Client".
  - A 400 uses the RFC 6749 error format: `error`, `error_description`, `error_uri`.
  - Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/postoauthtoken.md. The page's securityScheme `ApiClient` has `tokenUrl: /api/v1/oauth/token`.
- **Other sources for the path.** Jamf's recipe calls `"${url}/api/v1/oauth/token"` (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/recipes/client-credentials-authorization.md). [PD] lists `/v1/oauth/token` POST, privilege None, not deprecated.
- **Legacy path.** Jamf's blog says to use "the `/api/oauth/token` endpoint" (https://www.jamf.com/blog/understanding-jamf-pro-api-roles-and-clients/). Neither [PD] nor the 11.33 spec contains `/oauth/token` without `v1`. Use `/api/v1/oauth/token`. Whether the unversioned path still works is UNVERIFIED.
- **Version support.** From 10.49.0, "both the Classic and Jamf Pro APIs now support Client Credentials based authorization". "Access tokens can be used to interact with API endpoints in both the Classic and Jamf Pro APIs." Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/client-credentials.md

### Roles, secrets and lifetime

- **Role and secret changes.** "Adding or removing an API Role from an existing API Client requires that the client secret be rotated for the changes to take effect. Adding or removing a privilege from an API Role will immediately take effect for all newly generated access tokens." Source: the client-credentials guide above.
- **Secret retrieval.** "There is no way to retrieve an existing Client Secret, neither via the GUI nor the API." Source: the Jamf blog above.
- **Default lifetime.** The default `accessTokenLifetimeSeconds` is UNVERIFIED. No primary source states it. The OAuth reference page uses 60 as an example value, and the api-integrations page uses 300; neither is a default.

### Invalidation

- **Endpoint.** `POST /api/v1/auth/invalidate-token` with a Bearer token returns 204. [PD] lists privilege None and no deprecation.
  - Sources: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/post_v1-auth-invalidate-token.md and [PD].
  - Jamf's client-credentials recipe calls it with an OAuth token and checks for 204.
  - The legacy `POST /auth/invalidateToken` was deprecated on 2020-06-01 [PD].
- **Keep-alive.** `POST /api/v1/auth/keep-alive` exists (privilege None [PD]). A client-credentials pack should request a new token instead.
- **Basic auth.** Before 11.5.0, a username and password could call any Classic endpoint. From 11.5.0 they can only obtain a token, but an option in the UI could relax this. From 11.17.0 the restriction cannot be turned off. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/classic-api-authentication-changes.md
- **SSO.** "API authentication does not support the use of SSO." Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/jamf-pro-api-overview.md

### Rate limits

- **No built-in limit.** "Jamf Pro does not have a built-in solution to restrict or limit the number of API requests made over a given time interval."
- **Guidance.** "Limit your interactions with Jamf APIs to no more than 5 concurrent connections." Jamf recommends exponential backoff. For applications that do not need real-time data, run full inventory syncs "no more than once every 24 hours" and filter to devices that reported in the last day.
- Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/jamf-pro-api-scalability-best-practices.md
- **Load signal on Jamf Cloud.** `GET /api/v1/health-status` requires authentication but no privilege [PD].
  - It returns `{api, ui, enrollment, device, default}`. Each group holds `{thirtySeconds, oneMinute, fiveMinutes, fifteenMinutes, thirtyMinutes}`, all numbers.
  - Each value is an acceptance ratio from 0 to 1: "1 means all requests were accepted and 0 means all were denied". Jamf Cloud nodes do reject requests under load.
  - "Health status metrics are only available in Jamf Cloud". The documented responses are 200 and 404.
  - The status code returned for a denied request is UNVERIFIED; the page documents no 429 or 503.
  - Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-health-status.md

### Cloud versus on-prem

- **Detection.** `GET /api/v1/cloud-information` needs no authentication (`x-authentication-required: false`) and no privilege [PD]. It returns `{cloudInstance, rampInstance, fedRampInstance, govCloudInstance, managedServiceProviderInstance, highComplianceInstance, fipsEnabled}`, all booleans. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-cloud-information.md
- **Clustering.**
  - Jamf Cloud has "up to a 60 second delay" before new objects reach other nodes.
  - Sticky sessions use the `APBALANCEID` or `jpro-ingress` cookie. The name "may vary based on hosting region and infrastructure".
  - A read-only pack does not need them.
  - Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/docs/sticky-sessions-for-jamf-cloud.md
  - The guide gives no cluster refresh interval. The earlier "refreshes every minute" claim is not supported by the page and has been removed.
- **Change Management export** is on-prem only. See section 12.

---

## 1. SSO settings

- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v3/sso`
- **Privilege:** **Read SSO Settings** (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v3-sso.md; [PD])
- **`SsoSettingsV3` fields:**
  - `configurationType`: enum `SAML`, `OIDC`, `OIDC_WITH_SAML`
  - booleans, each defaulting to false: `ssoEnabled`, `ssoBypassAllowed`, `ssoForEnrollmentEnabled`, `ssoForMacOsSelfServiceEnabled`, `enrollmentSsoForAccountDrivenEnrollmentEnabled`, `groupEnrollmentAccessEnabled`
  - `groupEnrollmentAccessName`: string
  - `enrollmentSsoConfig`: `{hosts: [string], managementHint: string}`
- **`oidcSettings`:** `userMapping` (enum `USERNAME`, `EMAIL`), `jamfIdAuthenticationEnabled` (default true), `usernameAttributeClaimMapping` (enum `USERNAME`, `EMAIL`)
- **`samlSettings`:**
  - `idpProviderType`: enum `ADFS`, `OKTA`, `GOOGLE`, `SHIBBOLETH`, `ONELOGIN`, `PING`, `CENTRIFY`, `AZURE`, `OTHER`
  - `metadataSource`: enum `URL`, `FILE`, `UNKNOWN`
  - `sessionTimeout`: integer, default 480
  - `tokenExpirationDisabled`: boolean, default false
  - `userAttributeEnabled`: boolean
  - strings: `userAttributeName`, `userMapping` (enum `USERNAME`, `EMAIL`), `groupAttributeName` (default `http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/claims/Group`), `groupRdnKey`, `idpUrl`, `entityId`, `metadataFileName`, `otherProviderTypeName`, `federationMetadataFile`
- **What `ssoBypassAllowed` means:** the spec does not describe the field.
  - Jamf's documentation describes the "Allow users to bypass the Single Sign-On authentication" option: users can sign in without SSO when they go straight to the Jamf Pro URL. Without it, unauthenticated users are redirected to the IdP.
  - Sources: https://learn.jamf.com/r/en-US/jamf-pro-documentation-current/Enabling_Single_Sign-On_in_Jamf_Pro and https://learn.jamf.com/r/en-US/jamf-pro-documentation-11.29.0/SAML-Based_Single_Sign-On (seen in search summaries, not fully opened).
  - Mapping the field to this checkbox is an inference: UNVERIFIED-strong.
- **Failover login:** `GET /api/v1/sso/failover` returns 200 `{failoverUrl: string, generationTime: integer}`, or 400 "Failover url not generated". Privilege: **Read SSO Settings**. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-sso-failover.md
  - Reading this privilege reveals the failover URL itself. Treat the value as sensitive and do not log it.
- **Related:** `GET /api/v2/jamf-pro-information` returns `ssoSamlEnabled` among other booleans. It requires authentication but no privilege [PD]. Its `byodEnabled` field is deprecated as of 11.25. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v2-jamf-pro-information.md
- **STIG link:** V-241791 (medium) requires a session lock after 15 minutes of inactivity. `samlSettings.sessionTimeout` (default 480) relates to it; that this field is the session lock is UNVERIFIED. Source: https://cyber.trackr.live/api/stig/Jamf_Pro_v10.x_EMM/3/2
- **Sample (illustrative):**
  `{"configurationType":"SAML","ssoEnabled":true,"ssoBypassAllowed":false,"ssoForEnrollmentEnabled":true,"samlSettings":{"idpProviderType":"AZURE","sessionTimeout":480,"tokenExpirationDisabled":false},"oidcSettings":{"userMapping":"USERNAME"}}`

## 2. API roles

- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/api-roles`, and `/{id}` for one role
- **Privilege:** **Read API Roles** (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/getallapiroles.md; [PD])
- **Parameters:** `page`, `page-size`, `sort` (default `id:asc`; fields `id`, `displayName`) and `filter` (fields `id`, `displayName`, for example `displayName=="*myRole*"`)
- **Response:** `{totalCount: integer, results: [{id: string, displayName: string, privileges: [string]}]}`
- **Catalogue of all privileges:** `GET /api/v1/api-role-privileges` returns `{privileges: [string]}`. Privilege: **Read API Roles**. [PD] also lists `/v1/api-role-privileges/search`. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-api-role-privileges.md
- **Sample (illustrative):** `{"totalCount":1,"results":[{"id":"1","displayName":"Maester RO","privileges":["Read Computers","Read SSO Settings"]}]}`

## 3. API integrations (API clients)

- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/api-integrations`, and `/{id}` for one client
- **Privilege:** **Read API Integrations** (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-api-integrations.md; [PD])
- **Parameters:** `sort` (default `id:asc`) and `filter`; both accept `id` and `displayName`
- **`ApiIntegrationResponse` fields:**
  - `id`: integer
  - `displayName`: string
  - `enabled`: boolean
  - `authorizationScopes`: [string], the names of the assigned API roles
  - `appType`: enum `CLIENT_CREDENTIALS`, `NATIVE_APP_OAUTH`, `NONE`
  - `clientId`: string
  - `accessTokenLifetimeSeconds`: integer
- **Missing fields:** the schema has no created, last-used or secret-age field.
- **Sample (illustrative):** `{"totalCount":1,"results":[{"id":1,"displayName":"My API Integration","enabled":true,"authorizationScopes":["Maester RO"],"accessTokenLifetimeSeconds":300,"appType":"CLIENT_CREDENTIALS","clientId":"538878d4-..."}]}`

## 4. Jamf Pro user accounts and groups

### Accounts

- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/accounts`
- **Privilege:** **Read Accounts** (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-accounts.md; [PD])
- **Sort and filter fields:** `id`, `lastPasswordChange`, `failedLoginAttempts`, `username`, `realname`, `email`, `phone`, `ldapServerId`, `distinguishedName`, `siteId`, `privilegeLevel`, `changePasswordOnNextLogin`, `accountStatus`
- **Default sort is inconsistent:** the schema default is `username:asc`, but the description says `username:desc`.
- **`UserAccount` fields:**
  - `id`: string
  - `username`, `realname`, `email`, `phone`, `distinguishedName`: string
  - `ldapServerId`: integer, default -1. Reading -1 as a local account is inferred from the default.
  - `siteId`: integer, default -1
  - `accessLevel`: enum `FullAccess`, `SiteAccess`, `GroupBasedAccess`
  - `privilegeLevel`: enum `ADMINISTRATOR`, `AUDITOR`, `ENROLLMENT`, `CUSTOM`
  - `lastPasswordChange`: date-time
  - `changePasswordOnNextLogin`: boolean
  - `failedLoginAttempts`: integer
  - `accountStatus`: enum `Enabled`, `Disabled`
  - `accountType`: enum `DEFAULT`, `FEDERATED`, `MIGRATED`
  - `plainPassword`: string, used for writes
- **Example filters:** `privilegeLevel==ADMINISTRATOR;accountStatus==Enabled`, or `ldapServerId==-1`
- **Sample (illustrative):** `{"totalCount":1,"results":[{"id":"1","username":"admin","ldapServerId":-1,"siteId":-1,"accessLevel":"FullAccess","privilegeLevel":"ADMINISTRATOR","lastPasswordChange":"2017-07-21T17:32:28Z","changePasswordOnNextLogin":false,"failedLoginAttempts":0,"accountStatus":"Enabled","accountType":"DEFAULT"}]}`

### Groups

- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/account-groups`
- **Privilege:** **Read Account Groups** (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-account-groups.md; [PD])
- **Parameters:** `sort` (default `name:asc`) and `filter`; fields `id`, `name`, `siteId`, `ldapServerId`
- **`AccountGroupV1` fields:**
  - `id`, `name`: string
  - `accessLevel`, `privilegeLevel`: same enums as accounts
  - `siteId`, `ldapServerId`, `directoryGroupId`: string
  - `members`: `[{id, username, realname, email}]`
  - `privileges`: [string], for example `["Read Computers","Update Computers"]`

### Last login and sessions

- **Per-account:** `UserAccount` has no last-login field.
- **`GET /api/v1/last-login`:** privilege **Read Last Login**. Returns 200 `{lastLogin: date-time}` or 204, and takes no parameters. The description says only "Returns the date of the last login event", so whose login it reports is UNVERIFIED. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-last-login.md
- **`GET /api/v1/user-sessions/active`:** privilege **Read User**. Returns `[{username, sessionId, lastAccessedTime, creationTime, userAgent, ipAddress}]`. [PD] also lists `/v1/user-sessions/count`. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-user-sessions-active.md

### Classic alternative (not needed)

- `GET /JSSResource/accounts/userid/{id}` returns:
  - `enabled` ("Enabled"/"Disabled")
  - `access_level` ("Full Access"/"Site Access"/"Group Access")
  - `privilege_set` ("Administrator"/"Auditor"/"Enrollment Only"/"Custom")
  - `directory_user`, `ldap_server{id,name}`, `force_password_change`
  - `privileges{jss_objects, jss_settings, jss_actions, recon, casper_admin, casper_remote, casper_imaging}`
- Classic privilege: "Read - User accounts and groups" [CP]
- Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/findaccountsbyid.md

## 5. Console password policy and lockout

- **No API endpoint was found.** The current JPAPI index (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/jamf-pro-api/llms.txt, 1,428 lines, re-downloaded 2026-11-09) has no password-policy or lockout resource. Neither does the Classic index (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/classic-api/llms.txt). The only password-related JPAPI items are LAPS, the recovery lock, `POST /v1/user/change-password` and PKI. Treat a password-policy API as UNVERIFIED; it probably does not exist.
- **Account preferences are not the policy.** `/api/v3/account-preferences` (privilege None [PD]) and `/api/v2/account-preferences` (deprecated 2025-06-30 [PD]) hold the caller's own UI preferences. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v3-account-preferences.md
- **What the policy covers in the UI.** It sets lockout attempts, self-unlock, password length, age, reuse and complexity, and applies only to local accounts. Source: https://learn.jamf.com/r/en-US/jamf-pro-documentation-11.16.0/Configuring_the_Password_Policy (not re-opened in this check; carried over).
- **Possible proxy signals:** `failedLoginAttempts`, `lastPasswordChange` and `changePasswordOnNextLogin` on `/api/v1/accounts`.
- **STIG values** (Jamf Pro v10.x EMM STIG; https://cyber.trackr.live/api/stig/Jamf_Pro_v10.x_EMM/3/2 reports `"published": "2026-09-02"`; all medium):
  - V-241804: password length of 15
  - V-241805 to V-241808: at least one lowercase, uppercase, number and special character
  - V-241809: minimum lifetime of 24 hours
  - V-241810: maximum lifetime of 6 months
  - V-241811: no reuse for 5 generations
  - V-241812: disable local accounts after 35 days inactive
  - V-241813: limit of 3 consecutive invalid attempts
  - V-241817: local accounts created during installation must be disabled

## 6. Server version and latest release

- **Version:** `GET /api/v1/jamf-pro-version` returns `{version: string}`. Authentication is required but no privilege [PD]. Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v1-jamf-pro-version.md
- **Latest release:** no API exists for it.
  - The documentation's "current" alias shows "Jamf Pro Documentation 11.33.0" (https://learn.jamf.com/r/en-US/jamf-pro-documentation-current/Change_Management).
  - Community announcements report 11.33 GA, 11.33.1 and 11.33.3. These are secondary and were not re-verified:
    - https://community.jamf.com/release-announcements-177/jamf-pro-11-33-now-available-58978
    - https://community.jamf.com/release-announcements-177/jamf-pro-11-33-3-now-available-59123
- **Supported-version policy:** Jamf's lifecycle policy is UNVERIFIED.
  - STIG V-241798 (high, rule SV-241798r971326_rule, JAMF-10-000700) requires a supported version.
  - Its check and fix text list v10.13.1 to v10.18 with end of support "TBD", and allow "a newer version than on the list". The list is stale. Source: https://cyber.trackr.live/api/stig/Jamf_Pro_v10.x_EMM/3/2/V-241798
  - Suggestion: a pack parameter for the minimum version.
- **Cloud versus on-prem:** Jamf manages Jamf Cloud upgrades, so this check matters mainly on-prem. Detect the deployment with `/api/v1/cloud-information`.

## 7. User-initiated enrollment

- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v4/enrollment`
- **Privilege:** **Read User-Initiated Enrollment** (https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v4-enrollment.md; [PD])
- **Enrollment toggles (booleans, defaults in parentheses):**
  - `macOsEnterpriseEnrollmentEnabled` (false)
  - `iosEnterpriseEnrollmentEnabled` (true)
  - `iosPersonalEnrollmentEnabled` (false)
  - `accountDrivenUserEnrollmentEnabled`
  - `accountDrivenDeviceIosEnrollmentEnabled`
  - `accountDrivenDeviceMacosEnrollmentEnabled`
  - `accountDrivenUserVisionosEnrollmentEnabled`
  - `accountDrivenDeviceVisionosEnrollmentEnabled`
- **Other fields:**
  - booleans: `installSingleProfile`, `signingMdmProfileEnabled`, `restrictReenrollment`, `flushLocationInformation`, `flushLocationHistoryInformation`, `flushPolicyHistory`, `flushExtensionAttributes`, `flushSoftwareUpdatePlans`, `createManagementAccount` (default true), `hideManagementAccount`, `allowSshOnlyManagementAccount`, `ensureSshRunning` (default true), `launchSelfService`, `signQuickAdd`, `maidUsernameMergeEnabled`
  - `managementUsername`: string, the only required field
  - `flushMdmCommandsOnReenroll`: enum `DELETE_NOTHING`, `DELETE_ERRORS`, `DELETE_EVERYTHING_EXCEPT_ACKNOWLEDGED` (default), `DELETE_EVERYTHING`
  - `personalDeviceEnrollmentType`: deprecated as of 11.25; always returns "USERENROLLMENT"
  - certificate objects `mdmSigningCertificate` and `developerCertificateIdentity`, of type `CertificateIdentityV2{filename, keystorePassword, identityKeystore, md5Sum}`. The pack should ignore these fields and never log them.
- **LDAP restriction:** `GET /api/v3/enrollment/access-groups`
  - Privilege: **Read User-Initiated Enrollment**
  - Parameters: `sort` (default `name:asc`) and `all-users-option-first` (default false)
  - Returns `{totalCount, results:[{id, groupId, ldapServerId, name, siteId, enterpriseEnrollmentEnabled, personalEnrollmentEnabled, accountDrivenUserEnrollmentEnabled, requireEula}]}`
  - Source: https://developer.jamf.com/jamf-pro/reference/get_v3-enrollment-access-groups.md
  - The claim that the built-in "All LDAP Users" group cannot be deleted was not re-verified (UNVERIFIED).

- **Token invalidation:** call `POST /api/v1/auth/invalidate-token` at the end of a run; it returns 204. See section 0.

## Minimum read-only API role for the pack

These are JPAPI privilege strings, each confirmed on the endpoint's reference page and in [PD]:

- Read SSO Settings
- Read API Roles
- Read API Integrations
- Read Accounts
- Read Account Groups
- Read Last Login
- Read User (for active sessions)
- Read User-Initiated Enrollment
- Read Device Enrollment Program Instances
- Read Computer PreStage Enrollments
- Read Mobile Device PreStage Enrollments
- Read Computers
- Read Mobile Devices
- Read Retention Policy
- Read JSS URL
- Optional: Access Management Setting Read. Its endpoint returns only the ADE server UUID.

Classic resources need the Read form of macOS Configuration Profiles, Mobile Device (iOS) Configuration Profiles, Webhooks and Disk Encryption Configurations. The exact API role strings are UNVERIFIED; confirm them with `GET /api/v1/api-role-privileges`.

These endpoints need authentication but no privilege: `/v1/jamf-pro-version`, `/v2/jamf-pro-information`, `/v1/health-status`, `/v1/notifications`, `/v1/login-customization` and `/v1/auth/invalidate-token`. `/v1/cloud-information` needs no authentication at all.

Never grant "View Disk Encryption Recovery Key", "View Recovery Lock", "View Local Admin Password", "View Local Admin Password Audit History", or any Create, Update, Delete, Send or Dismiss privilege.

Note that Read SSO Settings exposes the SSO failover URL, and the Classic webhook read exposes a `password` field. The pack must not log either value.

## Summary of what is UNVERIFIED

- Whether `/api/oauth/token` still works. It is not in the 11.33 spec or [PD]; use `/api/v1/oauth/token`.
- The default `accessTokenLifetimeSeconds`.
- Any password-policy or lockout API; none exists in the current indexes.
- Whose login `/v1/last-login` reports.
- The maximum `page-size`.
