<#
.SYNOPSIS
Writes tests/frameworks/mscp.json, the catalogue of the NIST macOS Security Compliance Project (mSCP) rules, from a
checkout of usnistgov/macos_security.

.DESCRIPTION
The fleet compliance results of Jamf Pro's Compliance Benchmarks name each rule by its mSCP rule ID, such as
os_gatekeeper_enable. This catalogue lets Maester show each result under its rule, with the rule's CIS macOS, DISA
STIG, NIST SP 800-53, NIST SP 800-171 and CMMC references.

Only identifiers and facts are written: the rule ID, its section, the mSCP baselines it is in and its references.
No rule text is copied. mSCP is licensed CC BY 4.0 (Apple's vendor description text excluded); the pack's README
gives the attribution.

Needs the powershell-yaml module: Install-PSResource powershell-yaml.

.PARAMETER MscpPath
A checkout of https://github.com/usnistgov/macos_security.

.PARAMETER MacOSVersion
The macOS major version whose CIS benchmark and DISA STIG references are written as Related references.

.EXAMPLE
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/usnistgov/macos_security ../macos_security
./build/Update-MscpFramework.ps1 -MscpPath ../macos_security
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $MscpPath,
    [Parameter()] [ValidatePattern('^\d{2}$')] [string] $MacOSVersion = '27'
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Import-Module powershell-yaml

$root = (Resolve-Path $MscpPath).Path
$rulesPath = Join-Path $root 'rules'
if (-not (Test-Path $rulesPath)) { throw "$MscpPath has no rules folder. Point -MscpPath at a checkout of usnistgov/macos_security." }

# The release, for the framework's version: the newest heading of the changelog, such as "mSCP 2.0 Release 27.1".
$version = $null
$changelog = Join-Path $root 'CHANGELOG.md'
if (Test-Path $changelog) {
    $heading = Select-String -LiteralPath $changelog -Pattern '^#+\s*\[?([^\]\r\n]*Release[^\]\r\n]*|v?\d+\.\d+[^\]\r\n]*)' | Select-Object -First 1
    if ($heading) { $version = $heading.Matches[0].Groups[1].Value.Trim() }
}
if (-not $version) { $version = (git -C $root describe --tags --always 2>$null) }
if (-not $version) { throw 'Could not read the mSCP release from CHANGELOG.md or git.' }

# The baselines each rule is in, from the macOS baselines of this macOS version.
$baselineOf = @{}
$baselineFiles = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath (Join-Path $root 'baselines/macos') -Filter "*_macos_$MacOSVersion.0.yaml" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
foreach ($file in $baselineFiles) {
    $name = $file.BaseName -replace "_macos_$MacOSVersion\.0$", ''
    if ($name -eq 'all_rules') { continue }
    $baseline = Get-Content -LiteralPath $file.FullName -Raw | ConvertFrom-Yaml
    foreach ($section in $baseline.profile) {
        foreach ($rule in $section.rules) {
            if (-not $baselineOf.ContainsKey($rule)) { $baselineOf[$rule] = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new() }
            $baselineOf[$rule].Add($name)
        }
    }
}
if ($baselineOf.Count -eq 0) { throw "No macOS $MacOSVersion baselines in $root/baselines/macos. Pick another -MacOSVersion." }

$requirements = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
$files = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $rulesPath -Filter '*.yaml' -Recurse -FollowSymlink
foreach ($file in ($files | Sort-Object Name)) {
    $rule = Get-Content -LiteralPath $file.FullName -Raw | ConvertFrom-Yaml
    if (-not $rule.id -or -not $rule.platforms -or -not $rule.platforms.ContainsKey('macOS')) { continue }
    $refs = $rule.references
    $related = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
    foreach ($c in @($refs.nist.'800-53r5')) { if ($c -and $c -ne 'N/A') { $related.Add("nist-800-53-r5:$c") } }
    foreach ($c in @($refs.nist.'800-171r3')) { if ($c -and $c -ne 'N/A') { $related.Add("nist-800-171-r3:$c") } }
    foreach ($c in @($refs.disa.cmmc)) { if ($c -and $c -ne 'N/A') { $related.Add("cmmc-2:$c") } }
    $cisLevel = $null
    foreach ($c in @($refs.cis.benchmark."macos_$MacOSVersion")) {
        if ($c -match '^\s*([\d.]+)\s*(\(level (\d)\))?') {
            $related.Add("cis-apple-macos-$($MacOSVersion):$($Matches[1])")
            if ($Matches[3]) { $cisLevel = "L$($Matches[3])" }
        }
    }
    foreach ($c in @($refs.disa.disa_stig."macos_$MacOSVersion")) { if ($c -and $c -ne 'N/A') { $related.Add("disa-apple-macos-$MacOSVersion-stig:$c") } }
    foreach ($c in @($refs.cis.controls_v8)) { if ($c -and $c -ne 'N/A') { $related.Add("cis-controls-v8:$c") } }

    $requirement = [ordered]@{ Id = [string]$rule.id; Section = $file.Directory.Name }
    if ($baselineOf.ContainsKey($rule.id)) { $requirement.Baselines = @($baselineOf[$rule.id] | Sort-Object -Unique) }
    if ($cisLevel) { $requirement.CisLevel = $cisLevel }
    if ($related.Count) { $requirement.Related = @($related | Select-Object -Unique) }
    $requirements.Add($requirement)
}

$framework = [ordered]@{
    Framework    = 'mscp'
    Name         = 'NIST macOS Security Compliance Project'
    Version      = $version
    Url          = 'https://github.com/usnistgov/macos_security'
    License      = 'CC BY 4.0. Includes contributions from the US Government, the public and Apple Inc.'
    Requirements = $requirements
}
$out = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '../tests/frameworks/mscp.json'
$null = New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path (Split-Path $out) -Force
$framework | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $out -Encoding utf8NoBOM
Write-Host "Wrote $($requirements.Count) macOS rules of mSCP $version to $out."

<#
.SYNOPSIS
Writes tests/frameworks/disa-jamf-pro-stig.json, the catalogue of the DISA Jamf Pro v10.x EMM STIG, from DISA's
XCCDF file.

.DESCRIPTION
The tenant checks of the pack name the STIG rule they support in Control, such as
disa-jamf-pro-stig:V-241798. This catalogue gives Maester each rule's severity (CAT I to III), STIG ID and rule ID,
and its CCIs as Related references.

STIGs are works of the US Government and in the public domain. Download the STIG zip from
https://public.cyber.mil/stigs/downloads/ (search for Jamf), unzip it and pass the Manual-xccdf.xml file.

.PARAMETER XccdfPath
The U_Jamf_Pro_v10-x_EMM_STIG_V<n>R<n>_Manual-xccdf.xml file.

.EXAMPLE
./build/Update-JamfStigFramework.ps1 -XccdfPath ./REDACTED.xml
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param([Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $XccdfPath)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
[xml]$xml = Get-Content -LiteralPath $XccdfPath -Raw
$ns = [System.Xml.XmlNamespaceManager]::new($xml.NameTable)
$ns.AddNamespace('x', 'http://checklists.nist.gov/xccdf/1.1')
$benchmark = $xml.SelectSingleNode('/x:Benchmark', $ns)
if (-not $benchmark) { throw "$XccdfPath is not an XCCDF 1.1 benchmark." }

$release = $benchmark.SelectSingleNode("x:plain-text[@id='release-info']", $ns).InnerText
if ($release -notmatch 'Release:\s*(\d+)') { throw "Could not read the release from '$release'." }
$version = "V$($benchmark.SelectSingleNode('x:version', $ns).InnerText)R$($Matches[1])"
$date = if ($release -match 'Benchmark Date:\s*(.+)$') { $Matches[1].Trim() }

$category = @{ high = 'CAT I'; medium = 'CAT II'; low = 'CAT III' }
$requirements = foreach ($group in $benchmark.SelectNodes('x:Group', $ns)) {
    $rule = $group.SelectSingleNode('x:Rule', $ns)
    $ccis = @($rule.SelectNodes("x:ident[@system='http://cyber.mil/cci']", $ns) | ForEach-Object { "cci:$($_.InnerText)" })
    $requirement = [ordered]@{
        Id       = $group.id
        StigId   = $rule.SelectSingleNode('x:version', $ns).InnerText
        RuleId   = $rule.id
        Severity = $category[[string]$rule.severity]
    }
    if ($ccis) { $requirement.Related = $ccis }
    $requirement
}

$framework = [ordered]@{
    Framework    = 'disa-jamf-pro-stig'
    Name         = 'DISA Jamf Pro v10.x EMM STIG'
    Version      = $version
    Date         = $date
    Url          = 'https://public.cyber.mil/stigs/downloads/'
    Requirements = @($requirements)
}
$out = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '../tests/frameworks/disa-jamf-pro-stig.json'
$null = New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path (Split-Path $out) -Force
$framework | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $out -Encoding utf8NoBOM
Write-Host "Wrote $(@($requirements).Count) rules of the Jamf Pro STIG $version ($date) to $out."

function Get-JamfProMobileDevice {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns the inventory of every managed iPhone and iPad, with the GENERAL and SECURITY sections.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Reads GET /api/v2/mobile-devices/detail once per run, filtered to managed devices. LENIENT exception handling
    leaves out a section Jamf Pro cannot read for one device instead of failing the whole page. Needs the Read Mobile
    Devices privilege.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([object[]])]
    param()

    Get-JamfProPagedResult -Path 'api/v2/mobile-devices/detail' -Query 'section=GENERAL&section=SECURITY&exception-handling=LENIENT&filter=managed%3D%3Dtrue'
}

function Measure-JamfDevice {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Counts the devices that meet a condition, and writes the result of a fleet check.

    .DESCRIPTION
    The fleet checks all have the same shape: of the devices the check applies to, what share meets the
    requirement, against the lowest share the test accepts. This writes the Markdown result (the counts and a table
    of up to MaximumListed devices that do not meet it) and returns $true when the share is high enough.

    Skips the test when no device applies, with -NoDeviceReason.

    .PARAMETER Device
    The devices the check applies to.

    .PARAMETER Condition
    A script block that gets one device as $_ and returns $true when it meets the requirement.

    .PARAMETER Describe
    A script block that gets one device that fails as $_ and returns an ordered hashtable of the columns to show.

    .PARAMETER MinimumPercent
    The lowest share of devices, in percent, that must meet the requirement.

    .PARAMETER Requirement
    The requirement in a few words, such as "have FileVault on".

    .PARAMETER Noun
    The kind of device, such as Macs.

    .PARAMETER NoDeviceReason
    Why the test is skipped when no device applies.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [AllowEmptyCollection()] [object[]] $Device,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [scriptblock] $Condition,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [scriptblock] $Describe,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [int] $MinimumPercent,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Requirement,
        [Parameter()] [string] $Noun = 'Macs',
        [Parameter()] [string] $NoDeviceReason = 'Jamf Pro manages no device this check applies to.',
        [Parameter()] [int] $MaximumListed = 50
    )

    if ($Device.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason $NoDeviceReason
        return
    }

    $failing = @($Device | Where-Object { -not (& $Condition) })
    $meeting = $Device.Count - $failing.Count
    $percent = [math]::Floor(100 * $meeting / $Device.Count * 10) / 10
    $passed = $percent -ge $MinimumPercent

    $summary = "$meeting of $($Device.Count) $Noun ($percent%) $Requirement. The test needs at least $MinimumPercent%."
    $result = if ($passed -and $failing.Count -eq 0) { "Well done. All $($Device.Count) $Noun $Requirement." }
    elseif ($passed) { "Well done. $summary" }
    else { $summary }

    if ($failing.Count -gt 0) {
        $rows = @($failing | Select-Object -First $MaximumListed | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject](& $Describe) })

    A script block that gets one device that fails as $_ and returns an ordered hashtable of the columns to show.

    .PARAMETER MinimumPercent
    The lowest share of devices, in percent, that must meet the requirement.

    .PARAMETER Requirement
    The requirement in a few words, such as "have FileVault on".

    .PARAMETER Noun
    The kind of device, such as Macs.

    .PARAMETER NoDeviceReason

    #>

        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [scriptblock] $Describe,

function Connect-JamfPlatform {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Connects the pack to the Jamf Platform API, which serves the results of Jamf Pro's Compliance Benchmarks.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Connect-Maester -Service JAMF.Platform calls this. Its parameters come from -ServiceSetting, from
    Connections.JAMF.Platform in maester-config.json, or from MAESTER_JAMF_PLATFORM_<NAME> environment variables.

    The Platform API uses its own credentials, not the Jamf Pro API client: an integration in Jamf Account, scoped
    to the Jamf Pro environment, with only the compliance-benchmarks:read scope. Its environment ID is shown in the
    integration's details in Jamf Account. Compliance Benchmarks needs Jamf Cloud and Jamf Pro 11.16 or later.

    .PARAMETER Region
    The region of the Jamf Cloud instance: us, eu or apac.

    .PARAMETER ClientId
    The client ID of the Jamf Account integration.

    .PARAMETER ClientSecret
    The client secret of the integration. Prefer the MAESTER_JAMF_PLATFORM_CLIENTSECRET environment variable.

    .PARAMETER EnvironmentId
    The ID of the Jamf Pro environment, a GUID.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [ValidateSet('us', 'eu', 'apac')] [string] $Region,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $ClientId,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $ClientSecret,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [ValidatePattern('^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-([0-9a-fA-F]{4}-){3}[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$')] [string] $EnvironmentId
    )

    $state = @{
        Server        = [uri]"https://$($Region.ToLowerInvariant()).api.jamfcloud.com/"
        ClientId      = $ClientId
        ClientSecret  = REDACTED
        EnvironmentId = $EnvironmentId
        Cache         = @{}
    }
    Update-JamfPlatformToken -State $state
    Set-MtConnectionState -Service 'JAMF.Platform' -Value $state -Account "Jamf Account integration $ClientId" -Tenant "Jamf environment $EnvironmentId ($Region)"
}

function Test-JamfPlatform {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns $true when the pack has a Jamf Platform API token. The tests that need JAMF.Platform do not run otherwise.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    $state = Get-MtConnectionState -Service 'JAMF.Platform'
    [bool]($state -and $state.Token)
}

function Update-JamfPlatformConnection {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Gets a new Platform API token before the current one expires. Maester calls it as the connector's Renew function.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
    param()

    $state = Get-MtConnectionState -Service 'JAMF.Platform'
    if ($state -and $PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($state.Server.Host, 'Get a new Jamf Platform API token')) { Update-JamfPlatformToken -State $state }
}

function Disconnect-JamfPlatform {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Forgets the Platform API connection. Its token expires on its own after 15 minutes.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param()

    Clear-MtConnectionState -Service 'JAMF.Platform'
}

function Measure-JamfDevice {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Counts the devices that meet a condition, and writes the result of a fleet check.

    .DESCRIPTION
    The fleet checks all have the same shape: of the devices the check applies to, what share meets the
    requirement, against the lowest share the test accepts. This writes the Markdown result (the counts and a table
    of up to MaximumListed devices that do not meet it) and returns $true when the share is high enough.

    Skips the test when no device applies, with -NoDeviceReason.

    .PARAMETER Device
    The devices the check applies to.

    .PARAMETER Condition
    A script block that gets one device as $_ and returns $true when it meets the requirement.

    .PARAMETER Describe
    A script block that gets one device that fails as $_ and returns an ordered hashtable of the columns to show.

    .PARAMETER MinimumPercent
    The lowest share of devices, in percent, that must meet the requirement.

    .PARAMETER Requirement
    The requirement in a few words, such as "have FileVault on".

    .PARAMETER Noun
    The kind of device, such as Macs.

    .PARAMETER NoDeviceReason
    Why the test is skipped when no device applies.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [AllowEmptyCollection()] [object[]] $Device,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [scriptblock] $Condition,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [scriptblock] $Describe,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [int] $MinimumPercent,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)] [string] $Requirement,
        [Parameter()] [string] $Noun = 'Macs',
        [Parameter()] [string] $NoDeviceReason = 'Jamf Pro manages no device this check applies to.',
        [Parameter()] [int] $MaximumListed = 50
    )

    if ($Device.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason $NoDeviceReason
        return
    }

    $meetingDevices = @($Device | Where-Object -FilterScript $Condition)
    $failing = @($Device | Where-Object { $meetingDevices -notcontains $_ })
    $meeting = $Device.Count - $failing.Count
    $percent = [math]::Floor(100 * $meeting / $Device.Count * 10) / 10
    $passed = $percent -ge $MinimumPercent

    $summary = "$meeting of $($Device.Count) $Noun ($percent%) $Requirement. The test needs at least $MinimumPercent%."
    $result = if ($passed -and $failing.Count -eq 0) { "Well done. All $($Device.Count) $Noun $Requirement." }
    elseif ($passed) { "Well done. $summary" }
    else { $summary }

    if ($failing.Count -gt 0) {
        $rows = @($failing | Select-Object -First $MaximumListed | ForEach-Object -Process $Describe | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]$_ })
        $result += "`n`n$(ConvertTo-JamfMarkdownTable -InputObject $rows)"
        if ($failing.Count -gt $MaximumListed) { $result += "`n`nAnd $($failing.Count - $MaximumListed) more." }
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $result
    $passed
}

function Test-MPJAMF1001 {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that Jamf Pro administrators sign in through single sign-on (SSO) with the organisation's identity provider.
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id                 = 'MP.JAMF.1001',
        Title              = 'Jamf Pro administrators sign in with single sign-on',
        Product            = 'Jamf Pro',
        Feature            = 'Single sign-on',
        Area               = 'authentication',
        ResourceType       = 'Tenant',
        Severity           = 'High',
        UserImpact         = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Medium',
        Mitre              = ('T1078', 'T1110'),
        Control            = ('disa-jamf-pro-stig:V-241796', 'nist-800-53-r5:IA-2'),
        Service            = 'JAMF.JamfPro',
        Author             = 'merill'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    $sso = Invoke-JamfProRequest -Path 'api/v3/sso'

    if ($sso.ssoEnabled) {
        $provider = if ($sso.configurationType -eq 'OIDC') { 'OpenID Connect' }
        elseif ($sso.samlSettings.idpProviderType) { "SAML ($($sso.samlSettings.idpProviderType))" }
        else { [string]$sso.configurationType }
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "Well done. Single sign-on is turned on for Jamf Pro, with $provider."
        return $true
    }

    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result 'Single sign-on is turned off. Jamf Pro administrators sign in with passwords that Jamf Pro keeps, outside your identity provider''s MFA and Conditional Access.'
    $false
}

input.content:
Jamf Pro can control every Mac, iPhone and iPad it manages: it can install software, run scripts as root and
erase devices. Its administrators should sign in through your identity provider with single sign-on (SSO), so
that the provider's MFA, Conditional Access and account lifecycle apply to them, and leaving staff lose access to
Jamf Pro when their directory account is disabled.

Jamf Pro supports SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect (OIDC) single sign-on with providers such as Microsoft Entra ID,
Okta and Google.

This supports rule V-241796 of the DISA Jamf Pro STIG, which asks for console users to sign in with enterprise
accounts.

#### Remediation action

1. In Jamf Pro, go to **Settings** > **System** > **Single Sign-On** and click **Edit**.
2. Choose OIDC (with a Jamf Account) or SAML 2.0, and set up the connection to your identity provider.
3. Map your administrator groups from the identity provider to Jamf Pro groups with the right privileges.
4. Test sign-in with a second browser before you save, and keep one local break-glass account.

#### Related links

- [Jamf Pro documentation: Single Sign-On](https://learn.jamf.com/r/en-US/jamf-pro-documentation-current/Single_Sign-On)
- [DISA STIG library](https://public.cyber.mil/stigs/downloads/)

FileVault encrypts a Mac's startup disk, so the data on a lost or stolen Mac cannot be read without the user's
password or the recovery key. This test counts the Macs that Jamf Pro manages whose startup disk is encrypted, from
the FileVault status each Mac reports in its inventory. Macs that cannot report a status are left out.

It reports on rule `system_settings_filevault_enforce` of the NIST macOS Security Compliance Project, which the CIS
macOS benchmarks and the DISA macOS STIG also require.

#### Remediation action

1. In Jamf Pro, go to **Computers** > **Configuration Profiles** and open (or create) the profile that manages
   FileVault.
2. Add the **Security & Privacy** > **FileVault** payload (or **FileVault** in Jamf Pro 11), turn on **Require
   FileVault**, and escrow the personal recovery key to Jamf Pro.
3. Scope the profile to all managed computers, and check **Computers** > **Inventory** for Macs still not encrypted.
4. Raise or lower the share this test needs with the `MinimumPercent` parameter.

  name: 'jamf-pack-tests',
  description: 'Write and review the Jamf Pro pack checks in three groups',

const R = '/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-merill--claude-spares-spare-w9QrxL/f671424e-6754-4173-963b-f24a1e0ad80d/scratchpad/jamf'
const COMMON = `You are adding checks to a Maester Pack for Jamf Pro at /Users/merill/github/maester-pack-jamf (a PowerShell 7 pack; Maester source is at /Users/merill/github/maester, load it with Import-Module /Users/merill/github/maester/powershell/Maester.psd1).

Read first:
- The pack: maester-pack.json, connector/, helpers/ (every helper), tests/suite.json, tests/frameworks/*.json, and the two finished exemplar checks tests/Test.MP.JAMF.1001.ps1/.md (tenant setting) and tests/Test.MP.JAMF.1018.ps1/.md (fleet share via Measure-JamfDevice). Copy their structure and tone exactly.
- spec/Fixture.ps1 and spec/Pack.Tests.ps1: how checks are tested offline against recorded Jamf answers in the connection cache.
- Research on the Jamf APIs (endpoint paths, field names, enums, privileges), verified against Jamf's reference: ${R}/pro-api.md, ${R}/stig.md (every DISA Jamf Pro STIG rule and whether the API can check it), ${R}/benchmarks.md (Compliance Benchmarks / Platform API and mSCP). Raw OpenAPI pages are in ${R}/ref/. Use only fields these documents confirm.
- Maester's test-writing guide: /Users/merill/github/maester/website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx (attribute, parameters, families, Add-MtTestResultDetail, skips) and the attribute rubric /Users/merill/github/maester/website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md. Allowed Area and ResourceType keys are in /Users/merill/github/maester/powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1; valid ATT&CK IDs in /Users/merill/github/maester/powershell/assets/MaesterAttackTechniques.json.

Rules:
- Each check is tests/Test.MP.JAMF.<n>.ps1 (one function Test-MPJAMF<n> with a [MaesterTest(...)] attribute) plus tests/Test.MP.JAMF.<n>.md. Attribute: Id, Title (plain sentence stating the good state, no "(Preview)"), Product = 'Jamf Pro', Feature (short title-case free text, reuse the same Feature names across checks: 'Single sign-on', 'Administrator accounts', 'API clients', 'Server', 'Enrollment', 'Automated Device Enrollment', 'Webhooks', 'Disk encryption', 'Mac security', 'macOS updates', 'Inventory', 'Mobile device security', 'Compliance benchmarks'), Area and ResourceType from the taxonomy keys, Severity, UserImpact, ImplementationCost (rubric), Mitre (valid IDs, techniques the control prevents or detects), Control (first the requirement of a framework file the pack ships when one applies: 'disa-jamf-pro-stig:V-xxxxxx' or 'mscp:<rule id>' — the ID must exist in tests/frameworks/*.json; then 'nist-800-53-r5:<control>'), Service = 'JAMF.JamfPro' (or 'JAMF.Platform' for the Compliance Benchmarks family), Author = 'merill'.
- Read Jamf only through Invoke-JamfProRequest, Get-JamfProPagedResult (paged lists), Invoke-JamfPlatformRequest, Get-JamfProComputer, Get-JamfProMobileDevice, Get-JamfProAdministrator, Get-JamfProApiClient. Never call Invoke-RestMethod/Invoke-WebRequest. Results go through Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result (Markdown; use ConvertTo-JamfMarkdownTable for lists). Fleet shares use Measure-JamfDevice. You may add a helper in helpers/ (one function per file, Verb-Noun name with a Jamf prefix, comment-based help) when two or more checks need it; never edit helpers another group may use without keeping their behaviour.
- Pack files may hold only functions. Do not invoke script blocks with & or call a command whose name is computed (the pack's security scan flags it as DynamicCode): pass script blocks to Where-Object -FilterScript or ForEach-Object -Process instead.
- No connection checks and no outer try/catch in a check: the engine gates on Service and turns errors into Error rows. Use Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotApplicable (or Custom with -SkippedCustomReason) for conditions only the check can see (for example SSO turned off for a check that only applies with SSO). Use -Investigate when a person must judge the result.
- Parameters: thresholds with ValidateRange and a one-line # comment above each; string[] lists for exceptions (names of accounts or API clients). Defaults must make sense for most organisations.
- The .md: what the check looks at and why it matters (2 short paragraphs, plain direct sentences, no em-dash asides, no marketing words), the framework requirement it supports, then '#### Remediation action' with numbered steps naming the Jamf Pro UI path (Settings > ...), then '#### Related links' (learn.jamf.com pages you are confident exist, or developer.jamf.com), then a line '<!--- Results --->' and '%TestResult%'. Never copy STIG or CIS text verbatim beyond a short rule title.
- Tests for your checks go in your own spec file (named below), dot-sourcing spec/Fixture.ps1 in BeforeAll and calling Import-JamfSpecMaester. pack to a new version of ScubaGoggles, clone that release and run the generator:

```powershell
git clone --depth 1 --branch v1.1.0 https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGoggles ~/src/ScubaGoggles
. ./build/Update-ScubaGwsCatalog.ps1
Update-ScubaGwsCatalog -SourcePath ~/src/ScubaGoggles
```

The generator reads the baseline Markdown (`scubagoggles/baselines/*.md`), so a change to how CISA writes those
files can drop a field. The pack's tests ([spec/ScubaGogglesPack.Tests.ps1](spec/ScubaGogglesPack.Tests.ps1)), which
the pack check ([check-pack.yml](.github/workflows/check-pack.yml)) runs on Ubuntu and Windows, fail when a policy
has no title, criticality, rationale or remediation. They also run the pack on `spec/fixtures`, a cut of
ScubaGoggles' sample report with each result ScubaGoggles writes, and fail when one maps to the wrong Maester
Releases work as in the [demo pack](https://github.com/maester365/maester-pack-demo#versions-and-releases): with
the repository variable `PACK_RELEASES` set to `true`, every merged pull request gets the next version and a
release, with its notes from [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). Without it, `Install-MtPack` installs `main`.

## Files

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `maester-pack.json` | The manifest: ID, code, version, the suite, helpers and catalog |
| `maester-pack.guide.json` | How to install and run the pack, for its page on the pack index |
| `catalog.json` | The baselines' policies, generated by `build/Update-ScubaGwsCatalog.ps1` |
| `tests/` | The suite: the `MP.SCUBA.GWS` family test, with its instance source, and its Markdown |
| `helpers/` | Finding and reading the results file, the catalog, and turning ScubaGoggles' HTML into Markdown |

1	function Get-JamfComplianceBenchmarkRule {
2	    <#
3	    .SYNOPSIS
4	    Returns one instance per rule of every Jamf Compliance Benchmark, with the rule's results across its devices.
5	
6	    .DESCRIPTION
7	    Reads GET /compliance-benchmarks/v1/benchmarks and, for each benchmark, every page of
8	    GET /compliance-benchmarks/v1/benchmarks/{id}/rules through the Jamf Platform API. Rule IDs are mSCP rule IDs;
9	    a rule that the pack's mSCP framework file knows is mapped to it. When there is no benchmark, returns one
10	    instance that the test skips with how to create one.
11	    #>
12	    [CmdletBinding()]
13	    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
14	    param()
15	
16	    $benchmarks = @((Invoke-JamfPlatformRequest -Path 'compliance-benchmarks/v1/benchmarks').benchmarks | Where-Object { $_ -and [string]$_.syncState -ne 'DELETING' })
17	    if ($benchmarks.Count -eq 0) {
18	        return [pscustomobject]@{ Id = 'no-benchmarks'; Title = 'Jamf Compliance Benchmarks has no benchmark'; Data = $null }
19	    }
20	
21	    # The mSCP rules the pack's framework file knows, so an instance can name its requirement.
22	    $framework = Join-Path -Path $PSScriptRoot -ChildPath 'frameworks/mscp.json'
23	    $known = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([System.StringComparer]::Ordinal)
24	    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $framework) {
25	        foreach ($id in (Get-Content -LiteralPath $framework -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).Requirements.Id) { $null = $known.Add([string]$id) }
26	    }
27	
28	    $slugs = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)
29	    foreach ($benchmark in $benchmarks) {
30	        $title = [string]$benchmark.title
31	        $base = ($title.ToLowerInvariant() -replace '[^a-z0-9]+', '-').Trim('-')
32	        if ($base.Length -gt 40) { $base = $base.Substring(0, 40).Trim('-') }
33	        if (-not $base) { $base = 'benchmark' }
34	        # Two benchmarks with the same title still get IDs of their own.
35	        $slug = $base
36	        $n = 2
37	        while (-not $slugs.Add($slug)) { $slug = "$base-$n"; $n++ }
38	
39	        $rules = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
40	        $page = 0
41	        do {
42	            $response = Invoke-JamfPlatformRequest -Path "compliance-benchmarks/v1/benchmarks/$([uri]::EscapeDataString([string]$benchmark.id))/rules?page=$page&page-size=500"
43	            foreach ($rule in @($response.results)) { if ($null -ne $rule) { $rules.Add($rule) } }
44	            $page++
45	        } while (@($response.results).Count -gt 0 -and $rules.Count -lt [int]$response.totalCount)
46	
47	        $seen = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)
48	        foreach ($rule in $rules) {
49	            $ruleId = [string]$rule.ruleId
50	            $suffix = "$slug.$($ruleId -replace '[^A-Za-z0-9._-]', '-')"
51	            if ($suffix.Length -gt 128) { $suffix = $suffix.Substring(0, 128) }
52	            if (-not $seen.Add($suffix)) { continue }
53	
54	            $ruleTitle = if ($rule.ruleNumber) { "$($rule.ruleNumber) $($rule.ruleTitle)" } else { [string]$rule.ruleTitle }
55	            $instance = [ordered]@{
56	                Id     = $suffix
57	                Title  = $ruleTitle
58	                Fields = @{ Benchmark = $title; Section = [string]$rule.sectionName }
59	                Data   = $rule
60	            }
61	            if ($known.Contains($ruleId)) { $instance.Control = "mscp:$ruleId" }
62	            [pscustomobject]$instance
63	        }
64	    }
65	}

67	function Test-MPJAMF2001 {
68	    <#
69	    .SYNOPSIS
70	    Reports each rule of the Jamf Compliance Benchmarks as a result, from the share of devices that pass it.
71	    #>
72	    [MaesterTest(
73	        Id                 = 'MP.JAMF.2001',
74	        Title              = 'Devices pass the rules of Jamf Compliance Benchmarks',
75	        Product            = 'Jamf Pro',
76	        Feature            = 'Compliance benchmarks',
77	        Area               = 'devices',
78	        ResourceType       = 'Device',
79	        Severity           = 'Medium',
80	        UserImpact         = 'Medium',
81	        ImplementationCost = 'Medium',
82	        Mitre              = 'None',
83	        Control            = 'nist-800-53-r5:CM-6',
84	        Service            = 'JAMF.Platform',
85	        InstanceSource     = 'Get-JamfComplianceBenchmarkRule',
86	        Author             = 'merill'
87	    )]
88	    [CmdletBinding()]
89	    [OutputType([bool])]
90	    param(
91	        # One rule of a benchmark, supplied by the engine.
92	        $Instance,
93	
94	        # Lowest share of devices, in percent, that must pass a rule when some fail it.
95	        [ValidateRange(1, 100)]
96	        [int] $MinimumPassPercent = 100
97	    )
98	
99	    $rule = $Instance.Data
100	    if ($null -eq $rule) {
101	        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason 'Jamf Compliance Benchmarks has no benchmark. In Jamf Pro, go to Computers > Compliance Benchmarks, create a benchmark from an mSCP template and scope it to a smart computer group.'
102	        return
103	    }
104	
105	    $devices = [int]$rule.numberOfDevices
106	    if ($devices -eq 0) {
107	        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason 'No device in the benchmark''s scope has reported a result for this rule yet.'
108	        return
109	    }
110	
111	    $passed = [int]$rule.passed
112	    $failed = [int]$rule.failed
113	    $unknown = [int]$rule.unknown
114	    $percent = [math]::Round([double]$rule.passPercentage, 1)
115	    $counts = "| Passed | Failed | Unknown | Devices | Pass rate |`n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |`n| $passed | $failed | $unknown | $devices | $percent% |"
116	
117	    if ($unknown -ge $devices) {
118	        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "None of the $devices devices has reported whether it meets this rule. Check that the devices run macOS 15 or later and check in with Jamf Pro.`n`n$counts" -Investigate
119	        return $false
120	    }
121	    if ($failed -eq 0 -or $percent -ge $MinimumPassPercent) {
122	        $lead = if ($failed -eq 0) { "Well done. No device fails this rule." } else { "Well done. $percent% of devices pass this rule. The test needs at least $MinimumPassPercent%." }
123	        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "$lead`n`n$counts"
124	        return $true
125	    }
126	
127	    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "$failed of $devices devices fail this rule. The test needs at least $MinimumPassPercent% to pass, or no device to fail.`n`n$counts"
128	    $false
129	}

1	function Test-MPJAMF1025 {
2	    <#
3	    .SYNOPSIS
4	    Checks that enough Macs report no failed rule from the mSCP compliance script, through the extension attributes
5	    that the script, the Jamf Compliance Editor or Jamf Compliance Benchmarks write to inventory.
6	    #>
7	    [MaesterTest(
8	        Id                 = 'MP.JAMF.1025',
9	        Title              = 'Macs pass the mSCP compliance script',
10	        Product            = 'Jamf Pro',
11	        Feature            = 'Compliance benchmarks',
12	        Area               = 'devices',
13	        ResourceType       = 'Device',
14	        Severity           = 'Medium',
15	        UserImpact         = 'Medium',
16	        ImplementationCost = 'Medium',
17	        Mitre              = 'None',
18	        Control            = 'nist-800-53-r5:CM-6',
19	        Service            = 'JAMF.JamfPro',
20	        Author             = 'merill'
21	    )]
22	    [CmdletBinding()]
23	    [OutputType([bool])]
24	    param(
25	        # Lowest share of reporting Macs, in percent, that must have no failed rule.
26	        [ValidateRange(1, 100)]
27	        [int] $MinimumPercent = 90
28	    )
29	
30	    # One row per Mac that reports a result. A count attribute ("Compliance - Failed Results Count") leaves out
31	    # exempt rules, so it is used when the Mac has one; otherwise the failed rules in the list attributes
32	    # ("Compliance - Failed Result List", "<Benchmark> - Failed Result List") are counted, where empty means none.
33	    # A Mac whose count attribute is empty has not run the script yet and is left out, and so is a Mac whose
34	    # "Compliance - Version" attribute (written by the Jamf Compliance Editor) is empty.
35	    $reporting = foreach ($mac in (Get-JamfProComputer)) {
36	        $versions = @($mac.extensionAttributes | Where-Object { [string]$_.name -eq 'Compliance - Version' })
37	        if ($versions.Count -gt 0 -and -not @($versions | ForEach-Object { @($_.values) } | Where-Object { "$_".Trim() })) { continue }
38	
39	        $attributes = @($mac.extensionAttributes | Where-Object { [string]$_.name -match 'Failed Results? (Count|List)' })
40	        $countAttributes = @($attributes | Where-Object { [string]$_.name -match 'Failed Results? Count' })
41	        $counts = @($countAttributes | ForEach-Object {
42	                $text = (@($_.values) | Where-Object { "$_".Trim() } | Select-Object -First 1)
43	                $number = 0
44	                if ($null -ne $text -and [int]::TryParse("$text".Trim(), [ref] $number)) { $number }
45	            })
46	        $lists = @($attributes | Where-Object { [string]$_.name -match 'Failed Results? List' })
47	
48	        $failed = $null
49	        $source = $null
50	        if ($counts.Count -gt 0) {
51	            $failed = ($counts | Measure-Object -Sum).Sum
52	            $source = 'Failed Results Count'
53	        } elseif ($countAttributes.Count -eq 0 -and $lists.Count -gt 0) {
54	            $failed = @($lists | ForEach-Object { @($_.values) -join "`n" -split '[\r\n,;]+' } | Where-Object { $_.Trim() }).Count
55	            $source = 'Failed Result List'
56	        }
57	        if ($null -ne $failed) {
58	            [pscustomobject]@{ Name = [string]$mac.general.name; Failed = [int]$failed; Source = $source; LastContact = $mac.general.lastContact }
59	        }
60	    }
61	
62	    $measure = @{
63	        Device         = @($reporting)
64	        Condition      = { $_.Failed -eq 0 }
65	        Describe       = { [ordered]@{ Mac = $_.Name; 'Failed rules' = $_.Failed; 'Read from' = $_.Source; 'Last contact' = $_.LastContact } }
66	        MinimumPercent = $MinimumPercent
67	        Requirement    = 'have no failed mSCP rule'
68	        NoDeviceReason = 'No managed Mac has a Failed Results Count or Failed Result List extension attribute. Deploy the mSCP compliance script with the Jamf Compliance Editor, or set up Jamf Compliance Benchmarks, so Macs report their results to inventory.'
69	    }
70	    Measure-JamfDevice @measure
71	}

19	        Service            = 'JAMF.JamfPro',
20	        Author             = 'merill'
21	    )]
22	    [CmdletBinding()]
23	    [OutputType([bool])]
24	    param(
25	        # Lowest share of reporting Macs, in percent, that must have no failed rule.
26	        [ValidateRange(1, 100)]
27	        [int] $MinimumPercent = 90
28	    )
29	
30	    # One row per Mac that reports a result. A count attribute ("Compliance - Failed Results Count") leaves out
31	    # exempt rules, so it is used when the Mac has one; otherwise the failed rules in the list attributes
32	    # ("Compliance - Failed Result List", "<Benchmark> - Failed Result List") are counted, where empty means none.
33	    # A Mac whose count attribute is empty has not run the script yet and is left out, and so is a Mac whose
34	    # "Compliance - Version" attribute (written by the Jamf Compliance Editor) is empty.
35	    $reporting = foreach ($mac in (Get-JamfProComputer)) {
36	        $versions = @($mac.extensionAttributes | Where-Object { [string]$_.name -eq 'Compliance - Version' })
37	        if ($versions.Count -gt 0 -and -not @($versions | ForEach-Object { @($_.values) } | Where-Object { "$_".Trim() })) { continue }
38	
39	        $attributes = @($mac.extensionAttributes | Where-Object { [string]$_.name -match 'Failed Results? (Count|List)' })
40	        $countAttributes = @($attributes | Where-Object { [string]$_.name -match 'Failed Results? Count' })
41	        $counts = @($countAttributes | ForEach-Object {
42	                $text = (@($_.values) | Where-Object { "$_".Trim() } | Select-Object -First 1)
43	                $number = 0
44	                if ($null -ne $text -and [int]::TryParse("$text".Trim(), [ref] $number)) { $number }
45	            })
46	        $lists = @($attributes | Where-Object { [string]$_.name -match 'Failed Results? List' })
47	
48	        $failed = $null
49	        $source = $null
50	        if ($counts.Count -gt 0) {
51	            $failed = ($counts | Measure-Object -Sum).Sum
52	            $source = 'Failed Results Count'
53	        } elseif ($countAttributes.Count -eq 0 -and $lists.Count -gt 0) {
54	            $failed = @($lists | ForEach-Object { @($_.values) -join "`n" -split '[\r\n,;]+' } | Where-Object { $_.Trim() }).Count
55	            $source = 'Failed Result List'
56	        }
57	        if ($null -ne $failed) {
58	            [pscustomobject]@{ Name = [string]$mac.general.name; Failed = [int]$failed; Source = $source; LastContact = $mac.general.lastContact }
59	        }
60	    }
61	
62	    $measure = @{
63	        Device         = @($reporting)
64	        Condition      = { $_.Failed -eq 0 }
65	        Describe       = { [ordered]@{ Mac = $_.Name; 'Failed rules' = $_.Failed; 'Read from' = $_.Source; 'Last contact' = $_.LastContact } }
66	        MinimumPercent = $MinimumPercent
67	        Requirement    = 'have no failed mSCP rule'
68	        NoDeviceReason = 'No managed Mac has a Failed Results Count or Failed Result List extension attribute. Deploy the mSCP compliance script with the Jamf Compliance Editor, or set up Jamf Compliance Benchmarks, so Macs report their results to inventory.'
69	    }
70	    Measure-JamfDevice @measure
71	}

input.content:
# Jamf Pro pack for Maester

A [Maester Pack](https://maester.dev/docs/next/packs) that checks the security of a Jamf Pro server and of the
Macs, iPhones and iPads it manages. It reads Jamf Pro through its API and never changes anything.

- **The server:** single sign-on, administrator accounts, API clients, version, sign-in notice, enrollment and
  webhooks. Checks name the rule of the [DISA Jamf Pro v10.x EMM STIG](https://public.cyber.mil/stigs/downloads/)
  (V3R2, 30 Sep 2026) they support.
- **The fleet:** FileVault and recovery keys, System Integrity Protection, Gatekeeper, the firewall, macOS
  versions, check-in, passcodes, jailbreaks and iOS versions, from Jamf Pro's inventory. Mac checks name their rule
  of the [NIST macOS Security Compliance Project](https://github.com/usnistgov/macos_security) (mSCP, release
  27.1), which brings the CIS macOS benchmark, DISA macOS STIG, NIST SP 800-53 and CMMC references with it.
- **Compliance Benchmarks:** when you connect the Jamf Platform API too, each rule of your Jamf Compliance
  Benchmarks is a result of its own, mapped to its mSCP rule.

It needs Maester 3.0 or later and Jamf Pro 10.49 or later, on Jamf Cloud or your own server.

## Checks

| ID | Check | Severity | Framework rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MP.JAMF.1001 | Jamf Pro administrators sign in with single sign-on | High | STIG V-241796 |
| MP.JAMF.1002 | Users cannot bypass single sign-on | Medium | STIG V-241797 |
| MP.JAMF.1003 | Jamf Pro reaches the SAML identity provider over HTTPS | Medium | STIG V-241818 |
| MP.JAMF.1004 | Few accounts have full administrator access | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1005 | Only break-glass accounts sign in with a Jamf Pro password | Medium | STIG V-241817 |
| MP.JAMF.1006 | Local account passwords are changed within 180 days | Low | STIG V-241810 |
| MP.JAMF.1007 | No API client can read device secrets | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1008 | API clients that can change Jamf Pro are reviewed | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1009 | API client access tokens are short-lived | Low | |
| MP.JAMF.1010 | Jamf Pro runs a supported version | High | STIG V-241798 |
| MP.JAMF.1011 | The Jamf Pro sign-in page shows a use notice | Low | STIG V-241794 |
| MP.JAMF.1012 | User-initiated enrollment of Macs is off or limited to reviewed groups | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1013 | Computer PreStage enrollments keep the MDM profile on Macs | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1014 | Computer PreStage enrollments require the user to sign in | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1015 | Mobile device PreStage enrollments supervise devices and keep the MDM profile | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1016 | Automated Device Enrollment tokens are not about to expire | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1017 | Webhooks send over HTTPS with authentication | Low | |
| MP.JAMF.1018 | FileVault encrypts managed Macs | High | mSCP system_settings_filevault_enforce |
| MP.JAMF.1019 | FileVault recovery keys of encrypted Macs are escrowed and valid | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1020 | System Integrity Protection is on for managed Macs | Medium | mSCP os_sip_enable |
| MP.JAMF.1021 | Gatekeeper is on for managed Macs | High | mSCP os_gatekeeper_enable |
| MP.JAMF.1022 | The macOS firewall is on for managed Macs | Medium | mSCP system_settings_firewall_enable |
| MP.JAMF.1023 | Managed Macs run a supported macOS version | High | |
| MP.JAMF.1024 | Managed Macs check in with Jamf Pro | Low | |
| MP.JAMF.1025 | Macs pass the mSCP compliance script | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1026 | Managed mobile devices have a passcode that meets the profile | High | |
| MP.JAMF.1027 | No managed mobile device is jailbroken | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1028 | Managed iPhones and iPads run a supported iOS or iPadOS version | High | |
| MP.JAMF.2001 | Devices pass the rules of Jamf Compliance Benchmarks (one result per rule) | Medium | mSCP rule of each result |

Checks without a framework rule still name the NIST SP 800-53 controls they support. Most of the STIG is about the
server's operating system, database and firewall, or the console's password policy, which Jamf Pro's API does not
expose; the pack checks the 8 rules the API can show.

## Connect

### Jamf Pro

1. In Jamf Pro, go to **Settings** > **System** > **API roles and clients**.
2. On **API Roles**, create a role named `Maester (read only)` with these privileges:

   | Privilege | Used by |
   | --- | --- |
   | Read SSO Settings | 1001, 1002, 1003, 1005 |
   | Read Accounts | 1004, 1005, 1006 |
   | Read Account Groups | 1004 |
   | Read API Roles | 1007, 1008 |
   | Read API Integrations | 1007, 1008, 1009 |
   | Read User-Initiated Enrollment | 1012 |
   | Read Computer PreStage Enrollments | 1013, 1014 |
   | Read Mobile Device PreStage Enrollments | 1015 |
   | Read Device Enrollment Program Instances | 1016 |
   | Read Webhooks | 1017 |
   | Read Computers | 1018 to 1025 |
   | Read Mobile Devices | 1026 to 1028 |

   The version, cloud information and sign-in notice (1010, 1011) need no privilege. Never give the role a
   Create, Update, Delete or View privilege: the pack does not need one. A check whose privilege is missing
   reports an Error that names the API path it could not read.
3. On **API Clients**, create a client with that role, enable it, and generate a client secret. Note the client ID
   and secret.
4. Connect Maester. Keep the secret in an environment variable rather than in a file:

```powershell
Install-MtPack maester365/maester-pack-jamf
$env:MAESTER_JAMF_JAMFPRO_CLIENTSECRET = 'REDACTED'
Connect-Maester -Service JAMF.JamfPro -ServiceSetting @{ Server = 'https://contoso.jamfcloud.com'; ClientId = '<client id>' }
Invoke-Maester -Pack JAMF -SkipBuiltIn
```

The server can also be your own, such as `jamf.contoso.com:8443`. A Jamf Pro account works instead of an API
client (`Username` and `Password`), but API clients are the better choice: they have only the privileges you give
them and need no person's password.

### Jamf Compliance Benchmarks (optional)

MP.JAMF.2001 reads the results of [Compliance Benchmarks](https://learn.jamf.com/r/en-US/jamf-compliance-benchmarks-configuration-guide/Compliance_Benchmarks_Requirements)
through the Jamf Platform API. It needs Jamf Cloud and Jamf Pro 11.16 or later, and its own credentials:

1. In [Jamf Account](https://account.jamf.com), create an integration scoped to your Jamf Pro environment with only
   the `compliance-benchmarks:read` scope. Note the client ID, the secret and the environment ID shown in the
   integration's details. Integrations are valid for six months.
2. Connect:

```powershell
$env:MAESTER_JAMF_PLATFORM_CLIENTSECRET = 'REDACTED'
Connect-Maester -Service JAMF.Platform -ServiceSetting @{ Region = 'us'; ClientId = '<client id>'; EnvironmentId = '<environment id>' }
```

`Region` is `us`, `eu` or `apac`. MP.JAMF.2001 does not run until JAMF.Platform is connected.

## Run it in a pipeline

The pack signs in with a client secret, so it runs unattended. Set the connection in environment variables, which
`Connect-Maester` reads (`MAESTER_JAMF_JAMFPRO_<SETTING>` and `MAESTER_JAMF_PLATFORM_<SETTING>`):

```powershell
$env:MAESTER_JAMF_JAMFPRO_SERVER = 'https://contoso.jamfcloud.com'
$env:MAESTER_JAMF_JAMFPRO_CLIENTID = '<client id>'
$env:MAESTER_JAMF_JAMFPRO_CLIENTSECRET = 'REDACTED'
Connect-Maester -Service JAMF.JamfPro
Invoke-Maester -Pack JAMF -SkipBuiltIn -NonInteractive
```

Settings that are not secrets can go in `maester-config.json` instead:

```json
{ "Connections": { "JAMF.JamfPro": { "Server": "https://contoso.jamfcloud.com", "ClientId": "<client id>" } } }
```

## Settings

Thresholds and exceptions are test parameters. Set them per test under `TestSettings` in `maester-config.json`:

```json
{
  "TestSettings": [
    { "Id": "MP.JAMF.1005", "Parameters": { "BreakGlassAccounts": ["jamf-breakglass"] } },
    { "Id": "MP.JAMF.1018", "Parameters": { "MinimumPercent": 98 } }
  ]
}
```

| Check | Parameter | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MP.JAMF.1004 | MaximumAdministrators | 5 | Highest number of people with full administrator access |
| MP.JAMF.1005 | BreakGlassAccounts | none | Break-glass accounts that keep a Jamf Pro password; not counted |
| MP.JAMF.1005 | MaximumLocalAccounts | 2 | Highest number of other enabled local accounts |
| MP.JAMF.1006 | BreakGlassAccounts | none | Break-glass accounts whose password is not checked |
| MP.JAMF.1006 | MaximumPasswordAgeDays | 180 | Oldest a local account's password may be, in days |
| MP.JAMF.1007 | AllowedApiClients | none | API clients (name or client ID) allowed to read device secrets |
| MP.JAMF.1008 | AllowedApiClients | none | API clients reviewed and allowed to keep write privileges |
| MP.JAMF.1009 | MaximumTokenLifetimeSeconds | 1800 | Longest access token lifetime |
| MP.JAMF.1010 | MinimumVersion | 11.30.0 | Oldest Jamf Pro version accepted on a server you host |
| MP.JAMF.1016 | WarningDays | 30 | Days before a token expires that the check starts to fail |
| MP.JAMF.1017 | ExcludedWebhook | none | Webhooks that may send without HTTPS or authentication |
| MP.JAMF.1018 to 1027 | MinimumPercent | 95 or 100 | Lowest share of devices that must meet the check |
| MP.JAMF.1023 | MinimumMajorVersion | 15 | Oldest major macOS version that counts as supported |
| MP.JAMF.1024 | MaximumDaysSinceContact | 30 | Days without contact before a Mac counts as not checking in |
| MP.JAMF.1028 | MinimumMajorVersion | 26 | Oldest major iOS or iPadOS version that counts as supported |
| MP.JAMF.2001 | MinimumPassPercent | 100 | Lowest share of devices that must pass a benchmark rule when some fail |

Raise `MinimumVersion` and the two `MinimumMajorVersion` values as Jamf and Apple release new versions.

## How results map

Each check names its framework requirement in `Control`, and Maester adds the requirement's facts to the result's
`Benchmark`, so the report's framework view shows the pack's results under each rule:

- `disa-jamf-pro-stig:<Vuln ID>`, with the rule's STIG ID, rule ID, severity (CAT I to III) and CCIs, from
  [tests/frameworks/disa-jamf-pro-stig.json](tests/frameworks/disa-jamf-pro-stig.json).
- `mscp:<rule ID>`, with the mSCP baselines that include the rule and its CIS macOS, DISA macOS STIG, NIST SP
  800-53, NIST SP 800-171, CMMC and CIS Controls references, from
  [tests/frameworks/mscp.json](tests/frameworks/mscp.json).

The framework files hold identifiers and facts only, never the text of a rule.

## Maintaining the pack

Regenerate the framework files when a new release comes out:

```powershell
# mSCP: clone the release tag, then generate (needs the powershell-yaml module)
git clone --depth 1 --branch release_27.1 https://github.com/usnistgov/macos_security ../macos_security
./build/Update-MscpFramework.ps1 -MscpPath ../macos_security -MacOSVersion 27

# DISA Jamf Pro STIG: download and unzip it from https://public.cyber.mil/stigs/downloads/
./build/Update-JamfStigFramework.ps1 -XccdfPath ./REDACTED.xml
```

Then update the framework `Version` in [tests/suite.json](tests/suite.json).

The pack's tests in [spec/](spec/) run every check against recorded Jamf API answers, with no Jamf server:

```powershell
Invoke-Pester ./spec
```

Set `MAESTER_MODULE` to a `Maester.psd1` to test against a checkout of Maester. The pack check
([check-pack.yml](.github/workflows/check-pack.yml)) runs them on Ubuntu and Windows, and runs `Test-MtPack` on the
files the pack ships.

### Versions and releases

Releases work as in the [demo pack](https://github.com/maester365/maester-pack-demo#versions-and-releases): with
the repository variable `PACK_RELEASES` set to `true`, every merged pull request gets the next version and a
release, with its notes from [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). Without it, `Install-MtPack` installs `main`.

## Files

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `maester-pack.json` | The manifest: ID, code, connectors, suite and helpers |
| `maester-pack.guide.json` | How to install, connect and run the pack, for its page on the pack index |
| `connector/` | The JAMF.JamfPro and JAMF.Platform connectors: sign-in, token renewal and sign-out |
| `helpers/` | The one function that sends requests, cached reads of the APIs, and shared result formatting |

- **The server:** single sign-on, administrator accounts, API clients, version, sign-in notice, enrollment and
  webhooks. Checks name the rule of the [DISA Jamf Pro v10.x EMM STIG](https://public.cyber.mil/stigs/downloads/)
  (V3R2, 30 Sep 2026) they support.
- **The fleet:** FileVault and recovery keys, System Integrity Protection, Gatekeeper, the firewall, macOS
  versions, check-in, passcodes, jailbreaks and iOS versions, from Jamf Pro's inventory. Mac checks name their rule
  of the [NIST macOS Security Compliance Project](https://github.com/usnistgov/macos_security) (mSCP, release
  27.1), which brings the CIS macOS benchmark, DISA macOS STIG, NIST SP 800-53 and CMMC references with it.
- **Compliance Benchmarks:** when you connect the Jamf Platform API too, each rule of your Jamf Compliance
  Benchmarks is a result of its own, mapped to its mSCP rule.

It needs Maester 3.0 or later and Jamf Pro 10.49 or later, on Jamf Cloud or your own server.

## Checks

| ID | Check | Severity | Framework rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MP.JAMF.1001 | Jamf Pro administrators sign in with single sign-on | High | STIG V-241796 |
| MP.JAMF.1002 | Users cannot bypass single sign-on | Medium | STIG V-241797 |
| MP.JAMF.1003 | Jamf Pro reaches the SAML identity provider over HTTPS | Medium | STIG V-241818 |
| MP.JAMF.1004 | Few accounts have full administrator access | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1005 | Only break-glass accounts sign in with a Jamf Pro password | Medium | STIG V-241817 |
| MP.JAMF.1006 | Local account passwords are changed within 180 days | Low | STIG V-241810 |
| MP.JAMF.1007 | No API client can read device secrets | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1008 | API clients that can change Jamf Pro are reviewed | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1009 | API client access tokens are short-lived | Low | |
| MP.JAMF.1010 | Jamf Pro runs a supported version | High | STIG V-241798 |
| MP.JAMF.1011 | The Jamf Pro sign-in page shows a use notice | Low | STIG V-241794 |
| MP.JAMF.1012 | User-initiated enrollment of Macs is off or limited to reviewed groups | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1013 | Computer PreStage enrollments keep the MDM profile on Macs | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1014 | Computer PreStage enrollments require the user to sign in | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1015 | Mobile device PreStage enrollments supervise devices and keep the MDM profile | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1016 | Automated Device Enrollment tokens are not about to expire | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1017 | Webhooks send over HTTPS with authentication | Low | |
| MP.JAMF.1018 | FileVault encrypts managed Macs | High | mSCP system_settings_filevault_enforce |
| MP.JAMF.1019 | FileVault recovery keys of encrypted Macs are escrowed and valid | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1020 | System Integrity Protection is on for managed Macs | Medium | mSCP os_sip_enable |
| MP.JAMF.1021 | Gatekeeper is on for managed Macs | High | mSCP os_gatekeeper_enable |
| MP.JAMF.1022 | The macOS firewall is on for managed Macs | Medium | mSCP system_settings_firewall_enable |
| MP.JAMF.1023 | Managed Macs run a supported macOS version | High | |
| MP.JAMF.1024 | Managed Macs check in with Jamf Pro | Low | |
| MP.JAMF.1025 | Macs pass the mSCP compliance script | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1026 | Managed mobile devices have a passcode that meets the profile | High | |
| MP.JAMF.1027 | No managed mobile device is jailbroken | Medium | |
| MP.JAMF.1028 | Managed iPhones and iPads run a supported iOS or iPadOS version | High | |
| MP.JAMF.2001 | Devices pass the rules of Jamf Compliance Benchmarks (one result per rule) | Medium | mSCP rule of each result |

server's operating system, database and firewall, or the console's password policy, which Jamf Pro's API does not
expose; the pack checks the 8 rules the API can show.

## Connect

### Jamf Pro

1. In Jamf Pro, go to **Settings** > **System** > **API roles and clients**.
2. On **API Roles**, create a role named `Maester (read only)` with these privileges:

   | Privilege | Used by |
   | --- | --- |
   | Read SSO Settings | 1001, 1002, 1003, 1005 |
   | Read Accounts | 1004, 1005, 1006 |
   | Read Account Groups | 1004 |
   | Read API Roles | 1007, 1008 |
   | Read API Integrations | 1007, 1008, 1009 |
   | Read User-Initiated Enrollment | 1012 |
   | Read Computer PreStage Enrollments | 1013, 1014 |
   | Read Mobile Device PreStage Enrollments | 1015 |
   | Read Device Enrollment Program Instances | 1016 |
   | Read Webhooks | 1017 |
   | Read Computers | 1018 to 1025 |
   | Read Mobile Devices | 1026 to 1028 |

   Create, Update, Delete or View privilege: the pack does not need one. A check whose privilege is missing
   reports an Error that names the API path it could not read.
3. On **API Clients**, create a client with that role, enable it, and generate a client secret. Note the client ID
   and secret.
4. Connect Maester. Keep the secret in an environment variable rather than in a file:

```powershell
Install-MtPack maester365/maester-pack-jamf
$env:MAESTER_JAMF_JAMFPRO_CLIENTSECRET = 'REDACTED'
Connect-Maester -Service JAMF.JamfPro -ServiceSetting @{ Server = 'https://contoso.jamfcloud.com'; ClientId = '<client id>' }
Invoke-Maester -Pack JAMF -SkipBuiltIn
```

client (`Username` and `Password`), but API clients are the better choice: they have only the privileges you give
them and need no person's password.

1. In [Jamf Account](https://account.jamf.com), create an integration scoped to your Jamf Pro environment with only
   the `compliance-benchmarks:read` scope. Note the client ID, the secret and the environment ID shown in the
   integration's details. Integrations are valid for six months.
2. Connect:

```powershell
$env:MAESTER_JAMF_PLATFORM_CLIENTSECRET = 'REDACTED'
Connect-Maester -Service JAMF.Platform -ServiceSetting @{ Region = 'us'; ClientId = '<client id>'; EnvironmentId = '<environment id>' }
```

`Region` is `us`, `eu` or `apac`. MP.JAMF.2001 does not run until JAMF.Platform is connected.

```powershell
$env:MAESTER_JAMF_JAMFPRO_SERVER = 'https://contoso.jamfcloud.com'
$env:MAESTER_JAMF_JAMFPRO_CLIENTID = '<client id>'

```

```json

```

Thresholds and exceptions are test parameters. Set them per test under `TestSettings` in `maester-config.json`:

```json
{
  "TestSettings": [
    { "Id": "MP.JAMF.1005", "Parameters": { "BreakGlassAccounts": ["jamf-breakglass"] } },
    { "Id": "MP.JAMF.1018", "Parameters": { "MinimumPercent": 98 } }
  ]
}
```

| Check | Parameter | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MP.JAMF.1004 | MaximumAdministrators | 5 | Highest number of people with full administrator access |
| MP.JAMF.1005 | BreakGlassAccounts | none | Break-glass accounts that keep a Jamf Pro password; not counted |
| MP.JAMF.1005 | MaximumLocalAccounts | 2 | Highest number of other enabled local accounts |
| MP.JAMF.1006 | BreakGlassAccounts | none | Break-glass accounts whose password is not checked |
| MP.JAMF.1006 | MaximumPasswordAgeDays | 180 | Oldest a local account's password may be, in days |
| MP.JAMF.1007 | AllowedApiClients | none | API clients (name or client ID) allowed to read device secrets |
| MP.JAMF.1008 | AllowedApiClients | none | API clients reviewed and allowed to keep write privileges |
| MP.JAMF.1009 | MaximumTokenLifetimeSeconds | 1800 | Longest access token lifetime |
| MP.JAMF.1010 | MinimumVersion | 11.30.0 | Oldest Jamf Pro version accepted on a server you host |
| MP.JAMF.1016 | WarningDays | 30 | Days before a token expires that the check starts to fail |

I've built the Jamf Pro pack in `~/github/maester-pack-jamf`, set up like the ScubaGear and ScubaGoggles packs. All 126 spec cases pass against recorded Jamf API answers, and the shipped files pass `Test-MtPack -Official` at Medium risk. Nothing has run against a real Jamf server yet, and nothing is committed or pushed.

**What's in it**
- **Two connectors:**
  - **`JAMF.JamfPro`** signs in with a Jamf Pro API client or account and gets a new token before the old one expires.
  - **`JAMF.Platform`** is for Compliance Benchmarks. It needs a separate Jamf Account integration and only runs once you connect it.
- **28 checks plus one family:**
  - **Server:** single sign-on, SSO bypass, the identity provider over HTTPS, the number of full administrators, local break-glass accounts and their password age, API clients that can read device secrets or change Jamf Pro, token lifetime, version, sign-in notice.
  - **Enrollment and webhooks:** user-initiated enrollment, PreStage enrollments (MDM profile removable, sign-in required, supervision), enrollment token expiry, webhook HTTPS and authentication.
  - **Fleet:** FileVault and recovery-key escrow, System Integrity Protection, Gatekeeper, firewall, macOS and iOS versions, check-in, passcodes, jailbreaks, and results of the mSCP compliance script.
  - **MP.JAMF.2001:** one result per rule of your Jamf Compliance Benchmarks, each mapped to its mSCP rule.
- **Framework files**, generated by scripts in `build/`:
  - the DISA Jamf Pro STIG (V3R2, 29 rules)
  - mSCP release 27.1 (352 macOS rules), which carries the CIS macOS, DISA macOS STIG, NIST 800-53/171 and CMMC references
- **Repo files:** README (API role privileges, connect, settings), pack guide, CI workflows and a Pester spec that runs every check with no Jamf server.

**Limits you should know about**
- **The STIG mostly can't be checked remotely.** The API can show only about 8 of the 29 rules. The rest cover the server's operating system, database, firewall, or the console password policy, which has no API.
- **Some field meanings are inferred from their names.** Examples: `ssoBypassAllowed` as the "allow users to bypass SSO" option, and a local account read from its account type. The Classic API privilege name "Read Webhooks" is also unconfirmed. A run on a real server will settle these.
- **Version defaults will go stale.** The minimums are Jamf Pro 11.30.0, macOS 15 and iOS 26. They are parameters, so users can raise them.
- **MP.JAMF.2001 is untested against the live API.** Compliance Benchmarks only works on Jamf Cloud and its API is still labelled Beta.
- **Test code:** JAMF wasn't claimed on packs.maester.cloud when I checked.

Before any release, someone needs to run it against a Jamf Pro tenant, as you planned for ScubaGear.

# AGENTS.md

Maester is a PowerShell framework for monitoring Microsoft 365 security
configuration, with its own test engine. Pester is used only for the module's unit tests
and to run users' Pester-format custom tests. Requires PowerShell 7.4+. Monorepo: `powershell/` (module source),
`tests/` (security checks shipped to users), `src/Maester.Engine/` (C# engine core,
built DLL committed in `powershell/lib/`), `build/`, `website/` (Astro + Starlight,
maester.dev), `report/` (React app that builds the HTML report template).

## Two unrelated test trees — don't mix them

- `tests/` — Maester **security checks** that ship to end-user tenants, run via
  `Invoke-Maester`. Each check is a native test: `tests/<suite>/[<service>/]Test.<ID>.ps1`
  (one function with a `[MaesterTest(...)]` attribute) plus `Test.<ID>.md`. No
  `*.Tests.ps1` wrappers, no connection/licence guards, no outer try/catch: declare
  `Service`/`License` and the engine handles them. Scaffold with `New-MtTest`,
  validate with `Get-MtTest <ID>` (`Get-MtTest -Path` applies the rules of a custom test
  and does not report a missing attribute), run with `Invoke-MtTest -Path`; `Convert-MtTest`
  converts users' Pester-format tests. New MT.xxxx checks go here; follow
  `.github/skills/maester-test-expert/SKILL.md` and `website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx`,
  and choose the attribute values with `website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md`
  (see "Reviewing a test's attributes" below). A benchmark test for a requirement that another
  suite already checks is a shim that returns that test's result (see "Reviewing a test for
  duplicates" below).
- `powershell/tests/` — **unit tests for the module itself**.

## Commands

- Unit tests: `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1` — run before pushing. These enforce
  naming, exports, help, and PSScriptAnalyzer conventions; fix what they flag.
- Build module: `./build/Build-MaesterModule.ps1`; validate: `./build/Test-MaesterModuleOutput.ps1`
- Website: `cd website && npm ci && npm start` · Report: `cd report && npm ci && npm run build`

## Hard rules

- Generated content — regenerate, never hand-edit: `website/src/data/versions.json`, `website/versioned_docs/` (the frozen 2.x docs), everything under
  `powershell/internal/generated/`, and the native `tests/eidsca/Test.EIDSCA.*` and
  `tests/orca/Test.ORCA.*` files the generators in `build/eidsca/` and `build/orca/`
  write. Edit the PowerShell source, comment-based help or generator templates and let
  automation regenerate. `powershell/assets/MaesterServicePlanNames.json` (Microsoft's friendly name for each
  licence service plan) is written with `website/src/data/license-service-plans.json` by
  `website/scripts/update-license-service-plans.mjs`. `powershell/assets/ConsoleContributors.json` (the dashboard's
  Featured contributor list) is written by `./build/Update-ConsoleContributors.ps1` from
  the website's contributor data.
- Never commit the website data that each build generates: the command pages in `website/docs/commands/`
  (everything but `readme.mdx`), `website/src/data/test-catalog.json`, `contributors.json`, `sponsors.json`,
  `community-packs.json` and `catalog-history.json`. They are ignored by git. `website/scripts/prepare-data.mjs`
  writes them from the module source, the git history, GitHub and packs.maester.cloud before `npm run dev` and
  `npm run build`; `npm run refresh-data` writes them again.
  The build-website workflow builds and deploys maester.dev from main, so a merge needs no follow-up PR.
- A test is mapped to a framework in one place: the `Control` attribute, `<framework-key>:<requirement-id>`. A
  CIS test carries `Control = 'cis-m365:5.1.5.1'`, a CISA test `Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'`, and any other
  test may name the same requirements. An ASD test carries `Control = 'essential-eight:ISM-1504'` (or `ism:<id>` for a
  control outside the maturity model). Every test in `tests/cis`, `tests/cisa` and `tests/asd` must name a requirement of its
  suite's framework. The engine builds `Benchmark` from the first `Control` that a framework file knows and adds
  that requirement's `Related` references to `Control`; do not repeat those, and do not add benchmark tags.
- A framework file is a catalogue, not a list of tests: `tests/<suite>/frameworks/<key>.json`
  (`tests/cis/frameworks/cis-m365.json`, `tests/cis/frameworks/cis-github.json`,
  `tests/cisa/frameworks/cisa-scuba.json`, and the generated `tests/asd/frameworks/essential-eight.json` and
  `tests/asd/frameworks/ism.json`, written by `build/asd/Update-AsdFramework.ps1` from the ISM OSCAL release),
  declared in the suite's `suite.json` (`Frameworks`: `Key`,
  `Version`). It holds the framework's name and version and each requirement's `Id` and facts (CIS `Level` and
  `Profile`; CISA `Criticality`, `Upstream` and `Related` NIST references; Essential Eight `Level` and `Strategy`;
  ISM `Guideline`, `Section` and `Applicability`), never the text of a benchmark and
  never a `Tests` list. When a new test implements a requirement the file does not have, add the requirement in
  the same commit, or `./build/Build-MaesterModule.ps1` and the unit tests fail.
- Checks read through the session cache. A run reports on one snapshot of the tenant, so no check, pack or helper
  passes `-DisableCache` or otherwise bypasses the Graph or GitHub cache, even to read data that changed during the
  session. Only the transport helpers listed in `powershell/tests/general/GraphCacheUsage.Tests.ps1` may offer the
  switch, and that test fails on any other use. Don't apply a review suggestion to bypass the cache.

## Repository layout — where files go

Full rules and reasoning: `website/docs/contributing.md` ("Repository layout"), published at
https://maester.dev/docs/contributing#repository-layout. `powershell/tests/general/RepositoryLayout.Tests.ps1`
enforces them. When writing or reviewing a change, check every added, moved or renamed file:

- Folder names under `tests/`, `powershell/` and `build/` are lowercase kebab-case
  (`global-secure-access`, not `GlobalSecureAccess`). No two paths may differ only in case.
- One name per service, the same everywhere: `ad`, `azure`, `azure-devops`, `copilot`,
  `copilot-studio`, `defender`, `entra`, `exchange`, `fabric`, `foundry`, `github`,
  `global-secure-access`, `graph`, `intune`, `purview`, `sharepoint`, `teams`, `xspm`.
  Folders name the product whose settings a check reads, never a theme: an AI check goes in
  the folder of its product (an Entra agent identity check in `entra/`) and declares
  `Area = 'ai'`. A new service must be added to the guide and the test.
- `tests/<suite>/` holds only `Test.<ID>.ps1`, `Test.<ID>.md`, `suite.json` and `README.md`, plus the suite's
  framework files, `frameworks/<key>.json` beside its `suite.json` (lowercase key; nothing else goes in a
  `frameworks/` folder).
  Suites: `maester/<service>/` (plus `drift/`; `maester/xspm/` has its own suite.json),
  `cis/`, `cisa/<service>/`, `asd/<service>/`, `ad/<area>/`, generated `eidsca/` and `orca/`, and `custom/`
  (reserved for users; never commit tests there).
- `powershell/public/` (exported) is grouped by job: `run/`, `connect/`, `report/`, `app/`,
  `packs/`, `services/<service>/`. `powershell/internal/` uses `engine/`, `session/`, `connect/`,
  `report/`, `app/`, `packs/`, `services/<service>/`, `checks/<suite>/<service>/`, `generated/`,
  `utility/`. Nothing sits directly in `public/` or `internal/`.
- `packs/<name>/` at the repository root holds the Maester Packs that ship with Maester (ID `maester.<name>`,
  a code of the pack's own such as `ZTA`, test IDs `<Code>.<n>` without the `MP.` that installed packs use). They are not under `tests/`: a pack loads into its own private
  module, and its rows carry `Source = Custom` and `Package`. See `packs/README.md`.
- Put a function by its job, not by the check that first needed it: reusable data access
  for a service goes in `internal/services/<service>/`; logic only one suite's checks use
  goes in `internal/checks/<suite>/<service>/`; a helper users call from custom tests goes
  in `public/services/<service>/` (and in the manifest's `FunctionsToExport`).
- One function per file, named `Verb-Noun.ps1` after the function, with an approved verb.
- Custom tests can call only exported commands. To make an internal helper available to them,
  `git mv` it from `internal/services/<service>/` to `public/services/<service>/`, add it to
  `FunctionsToExport`, and give it full comment-based help (see "Making an internal helper public"
  in the contributing guide). Exporting a command makes it public API; flag a promotion in review.

## Reviewing a test for duplicates

Benchmarks overlap, and a check that CIS, CISA, ASD and Maester each implement in their own way gives
two answers for one setting and drifts with every benchmark update. When you write, change or review a
test, look for a duplicate before the attribute review:

1. Find the tests in every suite that read the same setting (`Get-MtTest -Product <key> -Feature <key>`,
   and a search of `tests/` for the Graph endpoint or setting name).
2. If one exists, read what the benchmark asks in its own sources, not only the requirement's one-line
   text: its audit or assessment guidance and any reference configuration it publishes (for ASD, the
   ISM, the Essential Eight assessment process guide and the ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud). Note
   every concrete value they name, and whether it differs from the existing test.
3. Decide, as "Tests that another suite already has" in `website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx` says:
   - the benchmark asks for what the existing test checks: the new test is a shim, a test whose body is
     `return <the existing test's function>`, with its own `Id`, `Title`, `Control` and guide;
   - it asks for the same check with a different value the existing test takes as a parameter: a shim
     that passes the value;
   - it asks for something no test checks, or a rule no parameter covers: a test of its own, which
     reads data through `powershell/internal/services/<service>/` helpers instead of copying another
     test's logic.
4. Fail the review when a benchmark test re-implements a check another suite already has and the
   benchmark's sources give no reason, or when a helper named after a suite (`Get-MtAsd*`,
   `Get-MtCis*`) does data access that is not specific to that suite. Say which test it duplicates
   and which source you read.

`powershell/tests/general/TestShims.Tests.ps1` checks the mechanical part: a shim declares the same
attribute values as the test it calls (`Product` to `Mitre`, `Service`, `License` and the other gates),
calls a test that exists and is not a shim, passes only parameters that test declares, leaves its own
requirement off that test's `Control`, and names that test in its guide. Whether the benchmark asks for
the same thing is the reviewer's judgement.

## Reviewing a test's attributes

Every built-in test declares what it is about, how urgent a failure is and which attack techniques
it addresses: `Product`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `Severity`, `UserImpact`,
`ImplementationCost`, `Mitre` and, where one applies, `RelatedProduct`. The rules for each value
are in `website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md` (the rubric); the allowed keys are in
`powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`.

When you write, change or review a test, check its attributes against the rubric as a separate
step, after the code review and before you approve or hand off:

1. Read the test's `.ps1` and `.md` and state in one sentence what it checks and what the fix is.
2. For each attribute that is new or changed, decide whether the declared value fits the rubric. A
   value fails only when the rubric clearly gives a different one; say which value and which rule.
3. Fail the review if any value does not fit. Do not approve with a note to fix it later.

Three things enforce this, in order:

- `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestAttributes.Tests.ps1` fails on anything mechanical: a missing
  attribute, a key that is not in the taxonomy, a retired ATT&CK technique, a taxonomy tag on a
  built-in test.
- The `attribute-review` workflow (`.github/workflows/attribute-review.yaml`) runs a reviewer model
  against the rubric on every pull request that adds a test or changes one of these attributes, and
  fails the check with the value it expected and the reason. It calls the Claude API with the
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` secret; without the secret it reports that the review was skipped. To run
  the same review locally before pushing, set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and run
  `./build/review/Invoke-MtAttributeReview.ps1 -BaseRef origin/main -OutputPath ./TestResults`
  (`TestResults/` is ignored by git; without `-OutputPath` the report is written to the current
  folder).
- The person or agent reviewing the pull request applies the same rubric and is the last word. A
  maintainer who disagrees with the workflow can apply the `attribute-review-override` label and
  should say why in the pull request.

## Labelling pull requests, issues and discussions

Labels follow one rubric so the queue can be filtered by status, type and product. The
labels are defined in `.github/labels.json`; the rules for choosing them are in
`.github/skills/maester-triage/SKILL.md`. To triage, use the `maester-triage` agent (or follow
the skill directly): it shows its plan before changing anything and only ever changes labels.
After editing `.github/labels.json`, run `./build/github/Sync-GitHubLabels.ps1` to see the
changes and `-Apply` to make them. `-Apply` creates, renames and updates labels and copies a merged
label onto the items that carry the old one; add `-DeleteMerged` to also delete the old labels.

## Agents and skills

The agents and skills in this repository are listed in `website/docs/agents-and-skills.md`. Each
has one source file: `.github/agents/<name>.agent.md` or `.github/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. The
Claude Code copies under `.claude/agents/` and `.claude/skills/`, and that docs page, are generated
from them by `./build/github/Update-AgentFiles.ps1`. Edit the source file, run the script, and
commit both; never edit a generated copy. `powershell/tests/general/AgentFiles.Tests.ps1` fails
when they drift.

- [Contributors attribution system](contributors-attribution-system.md) — registry + git-derived credits for maester.dev
- [Maester 3.0 design](maester-3-design.md) — design doc, owner rulings, status (M0–M9 done on PR 2334, design changes awaiting sign-off)
- [Maester Packs design](maester-marketplace-design.md) — packs/connectors marketplace draft + mockup; owner rulings 2026-10-07, some items open
